definition_en: a large farm in a warm region where one crop is grown for sale, historically worked by enslaved or forced labour; a planted area of trees; and an old word for a settlement or colony
core_image: 一排排茶树顺着山坡铺开，尽头是低矮的工棚
scene: 山坡上的茶树排成一行行，清晨的雾还没散。 Workers on the tea plantation began picking leaves before the mist lifted.
sceneCN: 这里 plantation 是「种植园」（第 1 个义项：大面积种植单一经济作物的农场）；句意为雾还没散，茶园里的工人就开始采叶了。图中可辨识物件：茶垄、山坡、低矮工棚。

derivatives.zh: 由 plant 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「种植者；种植园主」
由 plant 加 -ing 构成，义为「栽种；种植」

senses.title: A large farm growing one cash crop
senses.definition: a large farm in a warm region where a single crop such as cotton, sugar, tea or rubber is grown for sale, historically worked by enslaved or forced labour
senses.definitionCN: 气候温暖地区大面积种植棉花、甘蔗、茶叶或橡胶等单一作物以出售的大农场，历史上依靠奴役或强迫劳动耕作
senses.example: Workers on the tea plantation began picking leaves before the mist lifted.
senses.exampleCN: 雾还没散，茶园里的工人就开始采叶了。
senses.why: The word starts from planting, and when European powers planted one crop over huge tropical estates, the act of planting gave its name to the whole estate.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「栽种」开始；当欧洲列强在热带的大片土地上只种一种作物时，栽种这个动作就把名字给了整座农场。

senses.title: An area planted with trees
senses.definition: a piece of land where trees have been planted in rows, usually for timber or for a crop such as rubber
senses.definitionCN: 成行栽种树木的一片土地，通常为了木材或橡胶这类产出
senses.example: A narrow road runs through the plantation of young pines.
senses.exampleCN: 一条窄路穿过那片栽着幼松的人工林。
senses.why: Because planting is the core of the word, any piece of ground that people have deliberately filled with trees can be called a plantation, without any tropical crop.
senses.whyCN: 因为栽种是这个词的核心，任何被人有意种满树木的地块都能叫 plantation，并不需要热带作物。

senses.title: A settlement or colony
senses.definition: a settlement established by people who have moved into a region, especially an old colonial use of the word
senses.definitionCN: 迁入某地的人建立的定居点，尤指这个词在殖民时期的旧用法
senses.example: The old maps mark a small plantation on the river bank.
senses.exampleCN: 旧地图上标出了河岸边一处小小的移民地。
senses.why: To plant people is to settle them, so the same word could name a colony before it named a crop-growing estate, and that older sense survives in place names and history books.
senses.whyCN: 把人「种下」就是让他们定居，因此这个词先能指移民地，之后才指种植作物的农场；这层旧义还留在一些地名与历史书里。

intro.en: Plantation goes back to Latin planta, a sprout or a cutting, and its verb plantare, to set in the ground; French passed it on, and English widened it from planting to settlement and then to a whole estate.
intro.cn: plantation 上溯到拉丁语 planta（嫩芽、插条）及其动词 plantare（栽入土中）；法语把它传下来，英语又把它从「栽种」扩展到「移民地」，再扩展到整座农场。

items.en: Planta named a sprout, a cutting or a young shoot; it could also mean the sole of the foot, and the link between the two senses is uncertain.
items.cn: planta 指嫩芽、插条或幼枝，也可以指脚掌；这两种意思之间的联系来源不确定。

items.en: The verb plantare meant to set a cutting or a young plant in the ground, and so to establish something that will grow.
items.cn: 动词 plantare 意为把插条或幼苗栽进土里，因此也指建立起会生长起来的东西。

items.en: Plantatio was a planting or a set of plants, and it kept the idea of something deliberately placed and left to grow.
items.cn: plantatio 指一次栽种或一批种下的植物，保留着「有意放置、任其生长」的意思。

items.en: Old French plantation carried both the act of planting and a settlement, since settling people was pictured as planting them.
items.cn: 古法语 plantation 同时指栽种的行为和一处定居点，因为让人定居被比作把人种下去。

items.en: English first used plantation for a colony, then for the large single-crop estates of the Americas and the tropics, often worked by enslaved people.
items.cn: 英语先用 plantation 指殖民地，随后指美洲与热带地区大面积种单一作物的大农场，这些农场常常由被奴役的人耕作。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the plant family and two words that only share letters; the near-meaning group gathers kinds of landholding and groups of trees.
note.cn: 形近组收 plant 这一词族，另收两个只是字母相像的词；近义组收各类田产与成片树木。

entries.definition: A living thing that grows in soil, or to set it there; the Latin planta behind plantation is its source.
entries.definitionCN: 在土里生长的植物，或把它栽下；plantation 背后的拉丁语 planta 正是它的来源。

entries.definition: One who plants, or the owner of a plantation; it adds -er to the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 栽种的人，或种植园主；在同一个词干后加 -er。

entries.definition: A body orbiting a star; Greek planan, to wander, lies behind it, so the likeness is spelling alone.
entries.definitionCN: 绕恒星运行的天体；背后是希腊语 planan（漫游），只是拼写相像。

entries.definition: An aircraft or a flat surface; its roots are Latin planus and Greek aer, not Latin planta, so the two words are unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 飞机或平面；词根是拉丁语 planus 与希腊语 aer，并非 planta，与此词词源不同。

entries.definition: An area of land used for growing crops or keeping animals.
entries.definitionCN: 用于种作物或养牲畜的一片土地。

entries.definition: A large area of land in one ownership, often with a house.
entries.definitionCN: 归一人所有的大片土地，常带宅邸。

entries.definition: A large farm, especially one for cattle, in North America.
entries.definitionCN: 北美的大农场，尤指养牛的牧场。

entries.definition: A small group of trees growing together.
entries.definitionCN: 长在一起的一小片树林。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on the Latin noun for a cutting and the verb for setting it in the ground, and its family keeps the idea of something deliberately planted.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示插条的名词与表示栽入土中的动词上，词族始终带着「有意种下」的念头。

normal.en: Latin planta means a sprout or a cutting, so a plantation is literally a place where things have been set in the soil.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 planta 意为嫩芽、插条，所以 plantation 字面上就是「把东西种进土里的地方」。

normal.en: The verb plantare and the noun plantatio sit between planta and the English word, and all three share the same stem.
normal.cn: 动词 plantare 与名词 plantatio 夹在 planta 与英语词之间，三者共用同一个词干。

normal.en: French first used plantation for a settlement, which is why old maps and history books still speak of early colonies as plantations.
normal.cn: 法语最初用 plantation 指定居点，所以旧地图与历史书至今仍把早期殖民地叫作 plantation。

normal.en: Plant and plantation are related, but plane is not: plane comes from Latin planus, flat, not from planta.
normal.cn: plant 与 plantation 同源，但 plane 不是：plane 来自拉丁语 planus（平的），不是 planta。

normal.en: The suffix -ation turns the act of planting into the name of the place or the whole undertaking.
normal.cn: -ation 这个后缀把栽种的动作变成地点或整项事业的名称。

abstract.en: A plantation is an idea of order imposed on land: one crop, straight rows, a single purpose.
abstract.cn: 种植园是把秩序强加于土地的一种想法：一种作物、笔直的行列、单一的目的。

abstract.en: The same word once meant a home for newcomers and later meant a place built on forced labour, so its history carries both welcome and harm.
abstract.cn: 同一个词先指新来者的落脚地，后来指建立在强迫劳动之上的地方，它的历史里既有接纳也有伤害。

abstract.en: To plant is to trust the future enough to bury something now.
abstract.cn: 栽种就是足够相信未来，才肯把东西埋进此刻的土里。

examples.en: Workers on the tea plantation began picking leaves before the mist lifted.
examples.cn: 雾还没散，茶园里的工人就开始采叶了。

examples.en: The old cotton plantations along the river are now protected land.
examples.cn: 沿河那些旧棉花种植园如今成了受保护的土地。

examples.en: A narrow road runs through the plantation of young pines.
examples.cn: 一条窄路穿过那片栽着幼松的人工林。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普兰苔」——山坡上铺满兰草与苔藓，像一座种植园；记住 plantation 是种植园。

root: 拉丁语 planta（嫩芽、插条，也指脚掌）派生动词 plantare（栽种）与名词 plantatio（栽种），经古法语 plantation 进入英语；词义从「栽种、移民地」扩展到热带地区大面积种单一作物的大农场。plantation 与 plant 同源，与 plane 无关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is land where people have deliberately set plants; the senses run from the single-crop estate, to a planted stand of trees, and back to the older sense of a settlement.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是人有意种下植物的一片土地；义项从单一作物的大农场，走到成片栽种的树林，再回到更古老的「定居点」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: straight rows of tea bushes climbing a slope toward a low shed.
core.cn: 核心意象：笔直的茶垄顺坡而上，尽头是一间低矮的工棚。

branches.en: rows of tea bushes climbing a hillside
branches.cn: 顺山坡而上的茶垄

branches.en: baskets carried between cotton rows
branches.cn: 棉花行间挎着的筐

branches.en: young trees set in straight lines on bare ground
branches.cn: 空地上成行栽下的幼树

branches.en: a stand of pines planted after the old wood was cut
branches.cn: 老林砍伐后栽下的一片松树

branches.en: a small settlement marked on an old map
branches.cn: 旧地图上标出的小小定居点

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin noun for a cutting, its verb of planting, and the action noun those produced; French and English then added their own endings.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示插条的名词、表示栽种的动词以及它们造出的动作名词构成，法语与英语随后又加上各自的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Three Latin forms are recorded behind this word: the noun planta, the verb plantare, and the action noun plantatio.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后有三个可考的拉丁形式：名词 planta、动词 plantare，以及动作名词 plantatio。

definition_en: to give a person, animal or plant the food and care needed to grow, and to help an idea or feeling develop
core_image: 一只手把热汤稳稳送到嘴边，身体一点点有了力气
scene: 灶上的小火煨着一锅汤，母亲把勺子吹凉，再送到孩子嘴边，看着他慢慢有了血色。 Warm soup and steady care nourished the boy through a long winter.
sceneCN: 这里 nourish 是「滋养、养育」（第 1 个义项：供给养分让身体长起来）；句意为热汤与悉心照料让男孩熬过了漫长的冬天。图中可辨识物件：汤锅、勺子、灶火。

derivatives.zh: 由 nourish 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「营养；食物」
由 nourish 加 -ing 构成的形容词，义为「有营养的」
由表示「坏」的前缀 mal- 加 nourished 构成，义为「营养不良的」

senses.title: To give what the body needs for health
senses.definition: to provide a living thing with the food and substances it needs to stay healthy
senses.definitionCN: 给生物提供维持健康所需的食物与养分
senses.example: A balanced diet nourishes both body and brain.
senses.exampleCN: 均衡的饮食滋养身体和头脑。
senses.why: Latin nutrire meant to suckle and to feed, so the physical act of putting food into a body sits at the very centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nutrire 意为哺乳、喂养，所以「把食物送进身体」这个动作一直处在这个词的正中央。

senses.title: To feed and bring up a young person or animal
senses.definition: to care for a young person or animal until it can live on its own
senses.definitionCN: 照料幼小的生命，直到它能独立生活
senses.example: Her grandmother nourished her through a sickly childhood.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母把她这个体弱的孩子一手养大。
senses.why: Feeding a child is a single meal repeated day after day, so the same verb stretches from one serving of food to the whole work of raising someone.
senses.whyCN: 喂养孩子是一顿饭重复一天又一天，同一个动词便从「添一份饭」拉长成「把一个人养大」的全部工作。

senses.title: To help an idea or feeling grow
senses.definition: to keep a hope, feeling or relationship alive and growing
senses.definitionCN: 让希望、情感或关系保持活力并继续生长
senses.example: He nourished the hope of returning home one day.
senses.exampleCN: 他心里一直养着有一天回家的希望。
senses.why: An idea also needs to be fed; English borrows the bodily image and lets hopes and feelings be nourished as if they were living things.
senses.whyCN: 想法也需要被喂；英语借来身体层面的画面，让希望与情感像活物一样被滋养。

intro.en: Nourish goes back to a Latin verb for suckling and feeding, reached English through French, and now feeds bodies, soil, hopes and relationships alike.
intro.cn: nourish 可追溯到表示哺乳与喂养的拉丁动词，经法语进入英语，如今既喂养身体，也养护土壤、希望与关系。

items.en: Nutrire meant to suckle, to feed and to foster, already covering both the body and the person being raised.
items.cn: nutrire 意为哺乳、喂养、抚育，本已同时涵盖身体与被养大的人。

items.en: Nutrimentum named food and whatever feeds, and it stands behind the English words for nourishment.
items.cn: nutrimentum 指食物与养料，是英语中那组「营养」词汇的来源。

items.en: Old French nourrir meant to feed and to bring up, and it softened the Latin consonants on its way to English.
items.cn: 古法语 nourrir 意为喂养、抚育，在传入英语时软化了拉丁语的辅音。

items.en: Middle English nouren and nourishen kept both the feeding sense and the raising sense side by side.
items.cn: 中古英语的 nouren 与 nourishen 把喂养与抚养两层意思并排保留下来。

items.en: Modern English extends nourish to soil, skin, hopes and relationships, wherever something has to be kept alive.
items.cn: 现代英语把 nourish 扩展到土壤、皮肤、希望与关系，凡是需要维持生命的地方都能用。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family built on this verb; the near-meaning group collects verbs for feeding and supporting growth.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个动词构成的同族词；近义组收表示喂养与扶持成长的动词。

entries.definition: Food or whatever is needed for growth and health.
entries.definitionCN: 食物，或成长与健康所需的一切。

entries.definition: Badly fed, so that the body lacks what it needs.
entries.definitionCN: 吃得很糟、身体缺少所需养分的。

entries.definition: Not given enough food over a long period.
entries.definitionCN: 长期得不到足够食物的。

entries.definition: To give food to a person or animal.
To care for and encourage the growth of someone.
To keep something alive or going over time.
To help something develop gradually.

normalIntro.en: The word starts from milk and warmth, and everything it later feeds, from soil to a hope, is treated as something that must be kept alive.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从奶与温度开始，后来它所喂养的一切，从土壤到一个希望，都被当作必须维持生命的东西。

normal.en: Nutrire in Latin meant to suckle and feed, so nourish begins with milk and warmth rather than with abstract care.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 nutrire 意为哺乳、喂养，所以 nourish 的起点是奶与温度，而不是抽象的关心。

normal.en: Nourishment adds -ment to the verb and names what feeds, while the verb names the act of feeding.
normal.cn: nourishment 在动词后加 -ment，指「喂养的东西」，动词则指喂养这个动作。

normal.en: Malnourished puts mal-, bad, in front of nourished, so the body has been fed badly.
normal.cn: malnourished 在 nourished 前加表示「坏」的 mal-，指身体被喂得很糟。

normal.en: The same word feeds the body and feeds a hope, because English treats both as things that must be kept alive.
normal.cn: 同一个词既喂养身体，也滋养希望，因为英语把两者都当作必须维持生命的东西。

normal.en: Nourishing food is the plainest pairing, and the -ing form works directly as an adjective for whatever gives strength.
normal.cn: nourishing food 是最朴素的搭配，-ing 形式直接当形容词，指供给力气的东西。

abstract.en: A spoon held steady at a child's lips is the oldest picture of care that this word keeps.
abstract.cn: 一勺汤稳稳送到孩子嘴边，是这个词保存下来的最古老的照料画面。

abstract.en: What feeds the body and what feeds a hope obey one rule: something has to arrive regularly or the thing withers.
abstract.cn: 养身体的东西与养希望的东西遵守同一条规则：得定期送到，否则就会枯掉。

abstract.en: Nourish is a reminder that growing is not an event but a long series of small deliveries.
abstract.cn: nourish 提醒人：成长不是一件事，而是一长串小小的送达。

examples.en: A balanced diet nourishes both body and brain.
examples.cn: 均衡的饮食滋养身体和头脑。

examples.en: Her grandmother nourished her through a sickly childhood.
examples.cn: 祖母把她这个体弱的孩子一手养大。

examples.en: He nourished the hope of returning home one day.
examples.cn: 他心里一直养着有一天回家的希望。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「那瑞须」——那碗热汤里的细须，一口口把人养起来；nourish 就是滋养。

root: 一般认为来自拉丁语 nutrire（喂养、哺乳），经古法语 nourrir 进入英语；同族词多与「喂养、营养」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is feeding a living thing until it grows; the senses split between the body that is fed, the young that are raised, and the hopes and feelings that are kept alive the same way.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把食物喂给一个活物，让它长起来；义项分出三处：被喂养的身体、被养大的幼者，以及用同样方式维持着的希望与情感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holding a warm spoon steady at someone's lips while strength slowly returns.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把温热的勺子稳稳停在嘴边，力气一点点回到身上。

branches.en: a bowl of soup set down in front of a tired child
branches.cn: 一碗汤放在疲倦的孩子面前

branches.en: soil given compost before the planting season
branches.cn: 播种前施了堆肥的土

branches.en: a grandmother feeding a frail girl year after year
branches.cn: 祖母年复一年喂着瘦弱的小姑娘

branches.en: a hope kept alive through long waiting
branches.cn: 在漫长等待里被养着的希望

branches.en: the same steady feeding given to a body and to a dream
branches.cn: 同样稳定的喂养，一份给身体，一份给梦想

intro.en: The word carries a Latin verb of feeding plus two English suffixes that turn it into a thing and a quality, with the negative prefix marking the failure of that feeding.
intro.cn: 这个词带着表示喂养的拉丁动词，再加两个英语后缀，把它变成「物」与「性质」，否定前缀则标出喂养的失败。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: means or result of an act

definition_zh: 过滤器；滤光片；过滤；筛选
definition_en: a device that removes unwanted matter, a screen that changes light, to pass something through such a device, or to screen information
core_image: 咖啡一滴一滴穿过滤纸，落进下面的玻璃壶
scene: 咖啡慢慢通过滤纸滴进杯子里。 The coffee dripped through the paper filter into the cup.
sceneCN: 这里 filter 是「过滤器」（第 1 个义项）；句意：咖啡慢慢通过滤纸滴进杯子里。

senses.title: Straining device
senses.definition: a device that removes unwanted matter from liquid or air
senses.definitionCN: 从液体或空气中除去杂质的装置
senses.example: The coffee dripped through the paper filter into the cup.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡慢慢通过滤纸滴进杯子里。
senses.why: This is the basic device sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的装置义。

senses.title: Light screen
senses.definition: a screen that lets some light through and blocks the rest
senses.definitionCN: 让部分光通过而挡住其余光的镜片
senses.example: The photographer put a filter on the lens.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师在镜头上装了滤光片。
senses.why: The device sense extends to light.
senses.whyCN: 装置义扩展到光线。

senses.title: To strain
senses.definition: to pass liquid or air through a filter
senses.definitionCN: 使液体或空气通过过滤器
senses.example: They filter the water before drinking it.
senses.exampleCN: 他们喝水前先过滤。
senses.why: The noun turns into the action.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动作。

senses.title: To screen
senses.definition: to remove unwanted information or people
senses.definitionCN: 剔除不需要的信息或人员
senses.example: The software filters spam from email.
senses.exampleCN: 这款软件从邮件中筛除垃圾信息。
senses.why: Filtering applies to data as well as liquid.
senses.whyCN: 过滤也适用于数据，而不只是液体。

intro.en: Filter comes from Medieval Latin filtrum, felt, used as a strainer, through Old French filtre.
intro.cn: filter 出自中世纪拉丁语 filtrum（毛毡），因毛毡可用作滤材，经古法语 filtre 而来。

items.en: Filtrum meant felt used for straining.
items.cn: filtrum 指用于过滤的毛毡。

items.en: Filtre meant a strainer.
items.cn: filtre 意为过滤器。

items.en: Filter named a cloth or device for straining.
items.cn: 英语 filter 指过滤用布或装置。

items.en: Filters also treat air and engine fuel.
items.cn: 过滤器也用于处理空气与发动机燃料。

items.en: The verb extends to screening information.
items.cn: 动词形式扩展到筛选信息。

note.en: Filter is compared with similar-looking words and with words for straining and screening.
note.cn: 把 filter 与形近词以及表示过滤和筛选的词作比较。

entries.definition: something used to fill a space
to lose strength or confidence
liquid that has passed a filter
a device for separating solids from liquid
a mesh for separating fine matter
to check or block something

normalIntro.en: A filter lets what is wanted through and holds back the rest.
normalIntro.cn: 过滤器让需要的东西通过，把其余部分留下。

normal.en: A coffee filter holds the grounds.
normal.cn: 咖啡滤纸拦住咖啡渣。

normal.en: An air filter keeps dust out.
normal.cn: 空气过滤器挡住灰尘。

normal.en: Filter out means to remove.
normal.cn: filter out 意为滤除。

normal.en: The noun and verb look the same.
normal.cn: 名词与动词形式相同。

normal.en: A filtrate is what passes through.
normal.cn: filtrate 是透过滤器的液体。

abstract.en: To filter is to choose what may pass.
abstract.cn: 过滤就是选择什么可以通过。

abstract.en: Attention is a filter for a noisy world.
abstract.cn: 注意力是应对喧闹世界的过滤器。

abstract.en: What is held back can be as important as what gets through.
abstract.cn: 被挡住的东西可以和通过的一样重要。

examples.en: The coffee dripped through the paper filter into the cup.
examples.cn: 咖啡慢慢通过滤纸滴进杯子里。

examples.en: They filter the water before drinking it.
examples.cn: 他们喝水前先过滤。

examples.en: The software filters spam from email.
examples.cn: 这款软件从邮件中筛除垃圾信息。

dict_mnemonic.text: filter 出自中世纪拉丁语 filtrum（毛毡），因毛毡可作滤材，本义「滤布」，后指过滤器、滤光片与筛选。

root: 源自中世纪拉丁语 filtrum（毛毡），核心义「让一部分通过、拦住其余」。

sensesIntro.en: Filter means a straining device, a light screen, to strain, or to screen information.
sensesIntro.cn: filter 意为过滤器、滤光片、过滤或筛选。

core.en: A barrier that selects what passes.
core.cn: 挑选何物可通过的屏障。

branches.en: A device for liquid or air.
branches.cn: 用于液体或空气的装置。

branches.en: A screen for light.
branches.cn: 用于光线的镜片。

branches.en: The act of passing through.
branches.cn: 使之通过的动作。

branches.en: The act of screening data.
branches.cn: 筛选数据的动作。

branches.en: Liquid and information obey the same idea.
branches.cn: 液体与信息遵循同一观念。

intro.en: Filter belongs to the Medieval Latin filtrum family of straining.
intro.cn: filter 属于中世纪拉丁语 filtrum（毛毡）词族，关联过滤。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin filtrum is the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 filtrum 是历史词根。

items.exampleCN: 这家工厂使用三个过滤器。

items.example: Collect the filtrate in a jar.
The filterless pipe lets ash through.
items.exampleCN: 没有滤嘴的烟斗会漏进烟灰。

definition_zh: 和善地；亲切地；请（客套用语）
definition_en: in a warm and helpful way, and by courtesy in polite requests
core_image: 一个人半弯着腰，把门替身后的人扶住
scene: 地铁口风大，前面那人回头看了看后面提满东西的老人。 A young man kindly held the heavy door open for the crowded queue.
sceneCN: 这里 kindly 是「好心地、和善地」（第 1 个义项：以温暖体贴的方式），句意是个年轻人好心地替排队的人群扶住那扇很重的门。画面里有地铁口、大风和提满东西的老人。

pos.zh: 请；劳烦（用于客气的请求）
和善的；宜人的（较旧用法）

derivatives.zh: kindly 为 kind 加 -ly 构成，词基本身指和善的
由 kind 加 -ness 构成，指善意这个品质，与 kindly 分工不同
un- 加 kindly 构成，指不客气地、不厚道地
kindly 加 -ness 构成，指和蔼可亲的性质，多用于书面

senses.title: In a warm and helpful manner
senses.definition: with warmth and a willingness to help
senses.definitionCN: 带着温暖和乐于相助的态度
senses.example: She kindly carried the pram up the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 她好心地帮人把婴儿车抬上台阶。
senses.why: The -ly ending turns the adjective for a warm nature into the manner of acting that way.
senses.whyCN: -ly 把表示温和天性的形容词变成了以那种方式做事的样子。

senses.title: A polite request
senses.definition: used in requests to make them gentle and formal
senses.definitionCN: 用于请求中，使语气柔和而有礼
senses.example: Would you kindly keep your voice down?
senses.exampleCN: 劳烦您把声音放低一些好吗？
senses.why: A manner word placed in a command softens the command, and politeness became its own sense.
senses.whyCN: 把表示态度的词放进命令里就软化了命令，礼貌用法便自成一个义项。

senses.title: To accept or refuse politely
senses.definition: used in formulas to thank or refuse with courtesy
senses.definitionCN: 用于致谢或婉拒的固定客套说法
senses.example: Thank you kindly for the lift.
senses.exampleCN: 多谢您捎我一程。
senses.why: Fixed courteous formulas keep the old word alive long after it left ordinary speech.
senses.whyCN: 固定的客套说法让这个旧词在退出日常用语后依然存活。

senses.title: Of a gentle nature
senses.definition: adjective use meaning of a friendly and gentle disposition
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词用，指性情友善温和
senses.example: He gave me a kindly nod across the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 他在走廊那头和善地朝我点了点头。
senses.why: Before -ly became purely adverbial, it also made adjectives, as kindly still is in fixed turns.
senses.whyCN: 在 -ly 完全变成副词词尾之前，它也造形容词，kindly 在固定说法里仍作形容词。

senses.title: Speaking well of others
senses.definition: in the habit of speaking warmly about other people
senses.definitionCN: 习惯用好话谈论别人
senses.example: Everyone speaks kindly of the old doctor.
senses.exampleCN: 人人都说那位老医生的好话。
senses.why: The manner sense narrows to speech, where kindness is heard most often.
senses.whyCN: 态度义缩小到言语上，因为善意最常是在话里被听到的。

intro.en: Kindly is an adverb built from the old noun kind, meaning nature and family, with the English ending -ly.
intro.cn: kindly 由古名词 kind（意为天性、家族）加英语词尾 -ly 构成。

items.en: The base is gecynd, nature or inborn quality.
items.cn: 词基是古英语 gecynd，指天性、天生品质。

items.en: The form became kind, and an adjective sense of natural, then gentle, developed.
items.cn: 词形变为 kind，并发展出「合乎天性」进而「温和」的形容词义。

items.en: The ending -lic, later -ly, formed adverbs from adjectives and was written as kindeliche.
items.cn: 词尾 -lic 后作 -ly，用来把形容词变成副词，当时写作 kindeliche。

items.en: By the sixteenth century kindly meant in a warm, well-meaning way.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，kindly 已表示以温暖、善意的方式。

items.en: The polite request sense grew out of formal letters, where courtesy had to be written in.
items.cn: 客气的请求义从正式书信里长出来，那里礼貌必须写进字面。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the -ly and -ness relatives built on kind; the near-meaning group holds other words for acting in a warm way.
note.cn: 形近组收由 kind 加 -ly、-ness 的同族词；近义组收其他表示以温暖方式行事的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective and noun this adverb is built on.
entries.definitionCN: 这个副词所依附的形容词兼名词。

entries.definition: The quality of being kindly.
entries.definitionCN: 由 kindly 加 -ness 构成，指和蔼可亲的性质。

entries.definition: The negated adverb, meaning harshly.
entries.definitionCN: 加 un- 的否定形式，指不客气地。

entries.definition: With obvious friendliness and feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 指带着明显的友好和热意。

entries.definition: With courteous good manners.
entries.definitionCN: 指礼貌周到地，比 kindly 更正式。

entries.definition: With a free and giving spirit.
entries.definitionCN: 指大方慷概地，侧重给予而非态度。

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the adverb to its adjective, its opposite, and the polite formula it survives in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把这个副词和它的形容词、反义词以及它至今存活的客套话连起来。

normal.en: Kind is the adjective, kindly the adverb.
normal.cn: kind 是形容词，kindly 是副词。

normal.en: Unkindly adds un- for the opposite.
normal.cn: unkindly 加 un- 表反面。

normal.en: Kindliness keeps the -ness noun form.
normal.cn: kindliness 保留了 -ness 名词形式。

normal.en: Kindly in a request is only politeness, not a real description.
normal.cn: 请求句里的 kindly 只是礼貌，不是真实描述。

normal.en: Thank you kindly is older than thank you very much.
normal.cn: Thank you kindly 比 thank you very much 更老。

abstract.en: Kindly is holding a door you do not have to hold.
abstract.cn: 和善就是替人扶住一扇你本不必扶的门。

abstract.en: Politeness lives in fixed phrases long after people stop saying the word.
abstract.cn: 人们早就不说这个字了，礼貌却还住在固定说法里。

abstract.en: A manner word in a command is a hand on the shoulder rather than a finger in the face.
abstract.cn: 命令里放一个态度词，就是把手放上肩头而不是指着人鼻子。

examples.en: The nurse spoke kindly to the frightened child.
examples.cn: 护士和善地同受惊的孩子说话。

examples.en: Would you kindly close the window?
examples.cn: 劳烦您把窗户关上好吗？

examples.en: They treated the stranger kindly and gave him tea.
examples.cn: 他们善待那位陌生人，还给他倒了茶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「砍得利」——刀磨得利却不下手，转身替人扶门，就是好心

root: 古英语 gecynd（天性）→ 中古英语 kind，加副词词尾 -ly（古英语 -lic），由「合乎天性」转出「温和、好意地」；请求句中的用法源于正式书信的客套。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: acting warmly, the polite request, the courteous formula, the adjective use, and the habit of speaking well of people.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：以温暖方式行动、客气的请求、客套套语、形容词用法，以及习惯说人好话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand held on a heavy door for the person behind you.
core.cn: 核心意象：替身后的人扶住一扇沉重的门。

branches.en: THE NATURE LINE: a gentle disposition and its manner.
branches.cn: 天性这条线：温和的性情和它的方式。

branches.en: THE LETTER LINE: courtesy written into a request.
branches.cn: 书信这条线：写进请求里的客气。

branches.en: THE FORMULA LINE: thanks and refusals kept polite.
branches.cn: 套语这条线：致谢与婉拒保持有礼。

branches.en: THE TONGUE LINE: kindness heard in what is said about people.
branches.cn: 言语这条线：从谈论他人时听到的善意。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY LINE: the same warmth shown by the hand and by the voice.
branches.cn: 日常这条线：手上和声音里是同一种暖意。

intro.en: The word is a root plus an ending, so the items show the root, the ending, and the negated and nominal builds.
intro.cn: 这个词是词根加词尾，下面的条目展示词根、词尾以及加否定和名词化的形式。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic, and -ly corresponds to a Germanic suffix, so no Latin relatives exist.
latinIntro.cn: 词根属日耳曼语，-ly 也是日耳曼词尾，因此没有拉丁同族词。

items.exampleCN: 那是他最和气的一次回答。

items.example: Do not speak unkindly of them.

items.exampleCN: 她的和蔼立刻显了出来。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语「和善地、宽厚地」，与 kindly 只是意义相近

definition_en: easy to see or understand
core_image: 雨后的路上清晰的一串脚印
scene: 雨停后，泥地上的一串脚印清楚地说明有人来过。 After the rain stopped, a line of footprints in the mud made it evident that someone had been there.
sceneCN: 这里 evident 是「明显的」（第 1 个义项：容易看清或理解）；句意：雨停后，泥地上的一串脚印清楚地说明有人来过。

senses.title: Easy to see
senses.definition: easy to see or notice
senses.definitionCN: 容易看见或注意到
senses.example: The damage was evident at once.
senses.exampleCN: 损坏立刻就看出来了。
senses.why: Evident descends from Latin evidens, clearly seen.
senses.whyCN: evident 源自拉丁语 evidens（清楚可见的）。

senses.title: Easy to understand
senses.definition: clear to the mind
senses.definitionCN: 在思想上清楚明白
senses.example: It was evident that she was tired.
senses.exampleCN: 她显然累了。
senses.why: What is clear to the eye becomes clear to thought.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛看得清楚的事也变成思想上的明白。

senses.title: An obvious judgment
senses.definition: used to state a clear fact
senses.definitionCN: 用于陈述明显的事实
senses.example: His answer was evident to everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答对所有人来说都明摆着。
senses.why: The adjective often introduces an obvious judgment.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词常引出明显的判断。

intro.en: Evident comes from Latin evidens, clearly seen, from videre, to see.
intro.cn: evident 源自拉丁语 evidens（清楚可见的），来自 videre（看）。

items.en: Videre means to see.
items.cn: videre 意为看。

items.en: Evidens means clearly seen.
items.cn: evidens 意为清楚可见的。

items.en: French evident keeps the sense of clear.
items.cn: 法语 evident 保留了清楚的含义。

items.en: Evident describes what is easy to see.
items.cn: evident 描述容易看见的事物。

items.en: It also describes what is easy to understand.
items.cn: 它也描述容易理解的事物。

note.en: Evident stresses what the facts show; obvious stresses what no one can miss.
note.cn: evident 强调事实显示出来的清楚；obvious 强调谁都不会错过。

entries.definition: facts that prove something
clearly
relating to evidence
very easy to notice
easy to see or understand
easy to understand

normalIntro.en: Evident is a fact standing in plain sight.
normalIntro.cn: evident 是摆在明处的事实。

normal.en: Evident from the photo means the photo shows it.
normal.cn: evident from the photo 意为照片上看得出来。

normal.en: Clearly evident means very easy to see.
normal.cn: clearly evident 意为非常明显。

normal.en: Evident to all means everyone can see it.
normal.cn: evident to all 意为所有人都看得出来。

normal.en: Make it evident means show it clearly.
normal.cn: make it evident 意为把它清楚地显示出来。

normal.en: Compare obvious: evident comes from what is seen, obvious from what blocks the way.
normal.cn: 对比 obvious：evident 强调看见，obvious 强调挡在眼前无法忽视。

abstract.en: Picture clear footprints after rain.
abstract.cn: 想象雨后清晰的脚印。

abstract.en: Imagine a fact written in letters large enough to read from afar.
abstract.cn: 想象一个用远处也能看清的大字写出的事实。

abstract.en: Think of a curtain pulled back from a bright window.
abstract.cn: 想象明亮的窗帘被拉开。

examples.en: The reason for the delay was evident.
examples.cn: 延误的原因很明显。

examples.en: It was evident from her face that she had cried.
examples.cn: 从她脸上明显看得出她哭过。

examples.en: The improvement is evident in every chapter.
examples.cn: 每一章都能看出改进。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（出）＋ vident（看见）」——一眼就能看见，就是明显的。

root: 拉丁语 evidens（清楚可见的）← e-（出）＋ videre（看）→ evident，核心义「看得出来的」。

sensesIntro.en: Evident begins with what is easy to see, extends to what is easy to understand, and often states an obvious judgment.
sensesIntro.cn: evident 从容易看见开始，延伸到容易理解，也常用来陈述明显的判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: clear footprints left on a path after rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨后小路上清晰的脚印。

branches.en: What is easy to see comes first.
branches.cn: 容易看见是首要含义。

branches.en: What is easy to understand follows.
branches.cn: 容易理解紧随其后。

branches.en: The word often states an obvious fact.
branches.cn: 这个词常陈述明显事实。

branches.en: Sight and understanding share one clarity.
branches.cn: 看见与理解共享同一种清楚。

branches.en: A visible fact becomes an obvious judgment.
branches.cn: 可见事实变成明显判断。

intro.en: Evident comes from the Latin root vid, to see.
intro.cn: evident 来自拉丁词根 vid（看）。

latinIntro.en: Latin evidens is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 evidens 是直接来源。

definition_en: to make someone feel less confident, or to try to stop someone from doing something
core_image: 一只手刚抬起来要往前，另一只手从旁边轻轻把它按下去
scene: 报名表还摊在桌上，笔尖停在半空。 One failed attempt should not discourage you.
sceneCN: 这里 discourage 指「使气馁」（第 1 个义项：让人失去信心）；句意是一次失败不该让你泄气。

senses.title: To drain the will to try
senses.definition: to make someone feel less confident or less hopeful
senses.definitionCN: 让人失去信心或希望
senses.example: One bad grade should not discourage you.
senses.exampleCN: 一次糟糕的成绩不该让你气馁。
senses.why: Courage is a supply, and a few cold words can empty it.
senses.whyCN: 勇气像一份存量，几句冷话就能把它掏空。

senses.title: To talk someone out of an act
senses.definition: to try to stop someone from doing something by pointing at doubt or difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 用怀疑或困难让对方打消做某事的念头
senses.example: The teacher discouraged us from copying answers.
senses.exampleCN: 老师劝我们不要抄答案。
senses.why: A hand raised to stop is gentler than a door slammed shut.
senses.whyCN: 抬手拦住，比摔门关上要温和。

intro.en: Discourage joins dis-, meaning away, to the Latin cor, the heart, so the word pictures courage being taken out of the chest.
intro.cn: discourage 由表示「拿走」的 dis- 与拉丁语的心 cor 组成，画面是把勇气从胸口取走。

items.en: Cor, cordis meant the heart, and Romans placed courage there.
items.cn: cor 指心，罗马人把勇气安放在心里。

items.en: Descoragier meant to strip away heart or spirit.
items.cn: 古法语 descoragier 指把心气剥掉。

items.en: English borrowed it to mean deprive of courage.
items.cn: 英语借入后表示使失去勇气。

items.en: The sense widened to holding someone back from an act.
items.cn: 词义扩大，也指拦住别人不让做某事。

items.en: Today it covers both a lost heart and a friendly warning.
items.cn: 今天它既指心里泄气，也指好言拦阻。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the courage stem, while the meaning group gathers words for warning someone off.
note.cn: 形近组共享 courage 这一段，近义组则是几个表示劝退或泄气的词。

entries.definition: the strength to face fear
to give someone hope or support
the feeling of lost hope
to make someone decide not to act
to take away hope or spirit
to persuade someone not to do something

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the picture of a hand pressing another hand down.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子守住一幅画面：一只手把另一只手按下去。

normal.en: Dis- plus courage means courage taken out.
normal.cn: dis 加 courage，就是把勇气拿走。

normal.en: A coach who lists only failures discourages the whole team.
normal.cn: 教练只数落失败，整支队伍都会泄气。

normal.en: One cold comment can discourage a new learner.
normal.cn: 一句冷话就能让新学的人泄气。

normal.en: Friends discourage you from quitting by naming the risk.
normal.cn: 朋友点出风险，劝你别辞职。

normal.en: Discouraged parents stop asking the school for changes.
normal.cn: 心灰意冷的家长不再向学校提要求。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing another hand gently down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手轻轻把另一只手按下去。

abstract.en: Picture a balloon losing air until it lies flat.
abstract.cn: 想象一只气球漏气，最后瘪在地上。

abstract.en: Picture a voice at the door saying not yet.
abstract.cn: 想象门口有个声音说，再等等。

examples.en: Do not let one bad review discourage you.
examples.cn: 别让一条差评让你泄气。

examples.en: The rain discouraged most of the visitors.
examples.cn: 这场雨让大多数游客打消了念头。

examples.en: She was discouraged by the long waiting list.
examples.cn: 长长的等候名单让她泄了气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discourage 记成「抽走勇气」：dis 是拿走，courage 是勇气，勇气被拿走，人就泄气，也会劝人别做。

root: 来自古法语 descoragier，词根是拉丁语 cor（心），加前缀 dis- 表示拿走，本义是把心气抽走。英语里先指使人失去勇气，后也指用言语劝人放弃某件事。

sensesIntro.en: From a heart that loses its nerve, to a friend who talks you out of the plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一颗失去底气的心，到一位劝你放弃计划的朋友。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressed gently down on another hand as it starts to rise.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手刚刚抬起，另一只手轻轻把它按下去。

branches.en: The first sense is the inward loss of nerve.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是心里那点底气被抽走。

branches.en: The second sense turns that loss into advice for someone else.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这种泄气变成对别人的劝告。

branches.en: Both senses remove the will before the act begins.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在行动开始前先拿走意愿。

branches.en: Both can be caused by a single sentence from a stranger.
branches.cn: 两个义项都可能被陌生人的一句话造成。

branches.en: Only the second sense needs another person in front of you.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项需要眼前另有一个人才成立。

intro.en: Discourage gathers the courage family, with Latin cor, the heart, at its centre.
intro.cn: discourage 聚起 courage 一族，中心是拉丁语里表示心的 cor。

latinIntro.en: Latin cor, heart, gives cord- and courage; dis- and en- push the same stem in opposite directions.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cor（心）给出 cord 与 courage，前缀 dis- 与 en- 把同一词干推向相反方向。

items.meaning: the heart as the seat of bravery
items.example: It takes courage to speak first.
Her note encouraged the whole class.
He sounded discouraged on the phone.
items.exampleCN: 他在电话里听起来很泄气。

items.meaning: in a way that kills hope
items.example: She spoke discouragingly of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 她谈起这个计划时很泄气。

definition_zh: 多元文化的；包含或代表多种文化的；由不同族裔群体组成的；（政策、教育）面向多种文化的
definition_en: containing, representing or designed for several different cultures
core_image: 同一条街上并排开着面包房、寺院与外语报摊，每一扇门里都传出不同的语言
scene: 清晨的街区里，面包房、寺院与小报摊挤在同一条街上，招牌上的字各不相同， The city is multicultural, with bakeries, temples and newspapers from a dozen communities.
sceneCN: 这里 multicultural 指「包含并代表多种文化的」（第 1 个义项：一个空间里共存多种文化）；句意为这座城市是多元文化的，一条街上就有十几个社群的面包房、寺院与报纸。图中可辨识物件：面包房橱窗、寺院门廊、报摊、不同文字的招牌；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 多元文化的；包含多种文化的；面向多种文化的

derivatives.zh: 多元文化主义；多元文化政策
多元文化主义者；多元文化主义的

senses.title: Containing several cultures in one place
senses.titleCN: 同一空间里包含多种文化
senses.definition: containing or representing several different cultures within one society or place
senses.definitionCN: 在同一社会或地点内包含或代表多种不同文化
senses.example: The city is multicultural, with bakeries, temples and newspapers from a dozen communities.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市是多元文化的，一条街上就有十几个社群的面包房、寺院与报纸。
senses.why: The prefix adds many to the adjective of culture: one place now holds several ways of life at once.
senses.whyCN: 前缀把「多」加到「文化的」形容词上：同一个地点同时容纳好几种生活方式。

senses.title: Designed for several cultural groups
senses.titleCN: 为多个文化群体而设计的
senses.definition: planned or organized so that people from different cultural backgrounds can take part
senses.definitionCN: 为使不同文化背景的人都能参与而规划或组织的
senses.example: The school runs a multicultural education programme in four languages.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校用四种语言开设多元文化教育项目。
senses.why: Once an institution must serve several groups, the adjective moves from describing a place to describing a design.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一个机构必须服务多个群体，这个形容词就从描述地点转为描述设计。

senses.title: Made up of people of different origins
senses.titleCN: 由不同族裔来源的人组成
senses.definition: having a population drawn from several ethnic or national origins
senses.definitionCN: 人口来自多个族裔或国家来源
senses.example: The ward is multicultural: half its residents were born abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 这个选区是多元文化的：一半居民在国外出生。
senses.why: This sense counts people rather than traditions: the mix is in the population, not necessarily in a policy.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项数的是人，而不是传统：混杂在人口里，不一定在政策里。

senses.title: Reflecting several cultures in content
senses.titleCN: 在内容上反映多种文化
senses.definition: including material, images or voices from several cultures in a curriculum, book or exhibition
senses.definitionCN: 在课程、书籍或展览中纳入多种文化的材料、图像或声音
senses.example: The anthology is multicultural, pairing poets from three continents.
senses.exampleCN: 这本选集是多元文化的，把三个大洲的诗人放在一起。
senses.why: Here the many cultures appear as content to be read or seen, so the adjective qualifies a work rather than a society.
senses.whyCN: 这里多种文化作为可读、可看的内容出现，因此这个形容词修饰的是一部作品，而不是一个社会。

senses.title: Characterized by coexistence of traditions
senses.titleCN: 以多种传统共存为特征
senses.definition: marked by the peaceful coexistence of distinct traditions in daily life
senses.definitionCN: 以不同传统在日常生活中和平共存为特征
senses.example: The old quarter is multicultural, with processions that pass each other without conflict.
senses.exampleCN: 老城区是多元文化的，不同的游行队伍彼此交错而过，并不冲突。
senses.why: The adjective can describe a rhythm of daily life, not just a count of groups: coexistence is the feature being named.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词可描述日常生活的节奏，而不只是群体的数量：被命名的是「共存」这一特征。

senses.title: The official policy sense
senses.titleCN: 官方政策意义上的多元文化
senses.definition: relating to a state policy that officially recognizes and supports several cultures
senses.definitionCN: 与官方承认并支持多种文化的国家政策有关的
senses.example: Canada is often described as a multicultural state.
senses.exampleCN: 加拿大常被描述为多元文化国家。
senses.why: In this sense the adjective is a legal and political category, created when governments adopted multiculturalism as policy.
senses.whyCN: 在这个义项里，形容词是法律与政治范畴，是在政府把多元文化主义定为政策时才产生的。

senses.title: Mixing cultural forms in art
senses.titleCN: 艺术中混合多种文化形式
senses.definition: combining styles, genres or techniques drawn from different cultural traditions
senses.definitionCN: 把来自不同文化传统的风格、体裁或技法混合在一起
senses.example: Her multicultural collage joins calligraphy with electronic sound.
senses.exampleCN: 她的多元文化拼贴把书法与电子声音接在一起。
senses.why: The prefix can also work inside a work of art, where several traditions are deliberately placed side by side.
senses.whyCN: 这个前缀也可以在艺术品内部起作用，把好几种传统有意并置。

senses.title: Of a person formed by several cultures
senses.definition: describing a person whose upbringing or background has been shaped by more than one culture
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人的成长或背景受不止一种文化塑造
senses.example: She calls herself multicultural, cooking two cuisines and dreaming in two languages.
senses.exampleCN: 她说自己是多元文化的，会做两种菜系，也用两种语言做梦。
senses.why: The adjective can move from groups to one person: a single life may hold several cultural repertoires.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词可以从群体移到个人：一条生命里可以装着好几套文化本领。

intro.en: Multicultural joins Latin multus, many, with cultural, from Latin cultura, tilling and care. The compound is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: multicultural 由拉丁语 multus「多」与 cultural 结合而成，而 cultural 来自拉丁语 cultura「耕作、照料」。这是个现代复合词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Multus meant much or many. Its combining form multi- entered English through French and Latin and attaches freely to adjectives and nouns.
items.cn: multus 意为「多的、许多的」。它的组合形式 multi- 经法语与拉丁语进入英语，可自由附着在形容词与名词上。

items.en: Cultura, tilling and care, came from colere, to till or worship; English culture and cultural descend from it.
items.cn: cultura 意为耕作与照料，来自 colere「耕种、敬拜」；英语 culture 与 cultural 都由此而来。

items.en: English speakers combined the many-prefix with cultural once migration had made several cultures visible in one society.
items.cn: 当移民让多种文化在同一社会中变得可见，英语使用者就把表示「多」的前缀与 cultural 组合起来。

items.en: In the later twentieth century the adjective became a policy word in Canada and Australia, where official multiculturalism was adopted.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期，这个形容词在加拿大与澳大利亚成为政策用语，因为两地都采纳了官方的多元文化主义。

items.en: Schools, museums and critics then extended it to curricula, exhibitions and mixed artistic forms.
items.cn: 随后学校、博物馆与评论家又把它扩展到课程、展览与混合的艺术形式。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of the compound is dated differently, and the exact year when it became an official policy term is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个复合词在英语中的最早使用各家说法不一；它成为官方政策用语的确切年份也没有定论。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same stock that are often swapped; the second holds adjectives for mixing or variety.
note.cn: 第一组是同源、常被误换的词；第二组是表示混合或多样性的形容词。

entries.definition: The policy or ideology that supports several cultures; multicultural is the adjective describing a state or design.
entries.definitionCN: 支持多种文化的政策或意识形态；multicultural 是描述状态或设计的形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to culture in general or to one culture; it lacks the many-prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 与一般文化或某一种文化有关；它没有表示「多」的前缀。

entries.definition: Relating to interaction between cultures; multicultural describes several cultures coexisting inside one space.
entries.definitionCN: 与不同文化之间的互动有关；multicultural 描述多种文化在同一空间内共存。

entries.definition: Comparing or spanning cultures; it stresses the crossing, while multicultural stresses the mixture.
entries.definitionCN: 比较或跨越不同文化；它强调「跨越」，multicultural 强调「混合」。

entries.definition: Made up of several ethnic groups; it counts origins, while multicultural can also cover arts, policy and daily life.
entries.definitionCN: 由多个族裔群体组成；它数的是来源，而 multicultural 还可涵盖艺术、政策与日常生活。

entries.definition: Showing much variety of any kind; it does not specify that the variety is cultural.
entries.definitionCN: 显示出任何种类的丰富差异；它没有指明差异是文化上的。

entries.definition: Containing more than one element, often used of societies; it is broader and less specific than multicultural.
entries.definitionCN: 包含不止一个要素，常用于社会；比 multicultural 更宽、更不具体。

entries.definition: Made up of people and influences from many countries; it stresses international openness rather than internal cultural policy.
entries.definitionCN: 由许多国家的人与影响构成；它强调国际开放，而非内部文化政策。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real many-prefix, the real culture root and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示「多」的真实前缀、真实的 culture 词根，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: multi- means many, as in multiple and multimillion; cultural means of culture, so the word says many cultures at once.
normal.cn: multi- 表示「多」，如 multiple（多个的）与 multimillion（数百万的）；cultural 表示「文化的」，所以这个词说的是同时有多种文化。

normal.en: The family runs multicultural, multiculturalism, multiculturalist and multiculturally.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 multicultural（多元文化的）、multiculturalism（多元文化主义）、multiculturalist（多元文化主义者）、multiculturally（以多元文化的方式）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: multicultural society, multicultural education, multicultural policy, multicultural background.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：多元文化社会、多元文化教育、多元文化政策、多元文化背景。

normal.en: The word came of age when migration made several cultures visible in one city.
normal.cn: 当移民让多种文化在同一座城市里变得可见，这个词才真正成熟。

normal.en: Contrast the three prefixes: multi- is many inside, inter- is between, cross- is across.
normal.cn: 对照三个前缀：multi- 指内部有多个，inter- 指彼此之间，cross- 指横跨而过。

abstract.en: Picture one street holding several kitchens, each with its own smell.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街上开着好几家厨房，每家都有自己的气味。

abstract.en: Picture a curriculum with several voices speaking at once, none of them drowned out.
abstract.cn: 想象一份课程里有好几个声音同时说话，没有一个被淹没。

abstract.en: Picture a person carrying two languages in one mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人一张嘴里装着两种语言。

examples.en: The library serves a multicultural neighbourhood with books in nine languages.
examples.cn: 这家图书馆服务一个多元文化的社区，藏书有九种语言。

examples.en: A multicultural curriculum does not replace the canon; it widens it.
examples.cn: 多元文化课程并不取代经典，而是把经典的范围拓宽。

examples.en: The festival is multicultural in its music, food and costumes.
examples.cn: 这个节庆在音乐、食物与服饰上都是多元文化的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「多」加「文化的」——一个地方装下许多种文化，就是多元文化的。

root: 由拉丁语 multus「多」的组合形式 multi- 与 cultural 结合而成；cultural 来自拉丁语 cultura「耕作、照料」，再往前是 colere「耕种、敬拜」。这是现代英语复合词，colere 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one container: a place, a programme, a population, a text, a daily rhythm, a policy, an artwork and finally a single life all hold several cultures.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「容器」展开：地点、项目、人口、文本、日常节奏、政策、艺术品，最后连一条生命，都可以装着好几种文化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one street with several doors, each opening onto a different way of life.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条街上有好几扇门，每扇门后都是不同的生活方式。

branches.en: SPACE AND RHYTHM: several cultures share one place, and their traditions learn to pass one another without collision.
branches.cn: 空间与节奏：多种文化共享一个地点，它们的传统学会彼此交错而不相撞。

branches.en: DESIGN AND POLICY: a school programme and a state policy both organize the many cultures from above.
branches.cn: 设计与政策：学校的项目与国家的政策都从上方组织这多种文化。

branches.en: PEOPLE: the mixture can be counted in the population itself.
branches.cn: 人：这种混合可以直接在人口中数出来。

branches.en: CONTENT: a book or exhibition can hold the many cultures as material to be read and seen.
branches.cn: 内容：一本书或一场展览可以把多种文化作为可读、可看的材料装进去。

branches.en: MIXED FORMS AND LIVES: art can join traditions, and one person can carry several cultural repertoires.
branches.cn: 混合的形式与生命：艺术可以把传统接在一起，一个人也可以装着好几套文化本领。

intro.en: Multicultural is a many-prefix, a culture stem and an adjective ending, with further suffixes building the policy words.
intro.cn: multicultural 由一个表示「多」的前缀、一个 culture 词干与一个形容词词尾构成，后续词尾又造出政策类词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin multus supplies the many-prefix, cultura supplies the culture stem, and -alis supplies the adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 multus 提供表示「多」的前缀，cultura 提供 culture 词干，-alis 提供形容词词尾。

items.example: The stem also appears in multiple and multiply.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干也出现在 multiple（多个的）与 multiply（乘、增多）里。

items.example: The prefix builds multilingual and multiethnic.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀构成 multilingual（多语的）与 multiethnic（多族裔的）。

items.example: The noun became English culture through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词经法语成为英语 culture。

items.example: The ending builds cultural and natural.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 cultural（文化的）与 natural（自然的）。
这座城市是多元文化的。

items.meaning: the policy of supporting several cultures
items.meaningCN: 支持多种文化的政策或主义
items.example: The province adopted multiculturalism in the nineteen seventies.
items.exampleCN: 该省在二十世纪七十年代采纳了多元文化主义。

items.meaningCN: 多元文化主义的支持者
items.example: The multiculturalist defended the language programme.
items.exampleCN: 这位多元文化主义者为语言项目辩护。
这个街区在文化上是混合的。

items.example: Scholars debate the multiculturality of the old port.
items.exampleCN: 学者们争论这座老港口的多元文化状态。

derivatives.meaning: the doctrine or policy of several cultures

derivatives.meaningCN: 多元文化主义的支持者

definition_zh: 数学；数学学科；（某事物的）数学计算部分
definition_en: the branch of study that deals with numbers, quantities, shapes and the relations between them, using logical reasoning
core_image: 一整面黑板上密密的算式，粉笔灰落在槽沿，最后一行的等号被重重描了一遍
scene: 教室里一整面黑板写满算式，一名学生在角落补上一个等号，粉笔灰落在槽沿。 She studied mathematics for four years before turning to economics.
sceneCN: 这里 mathematics 指「作为一门学科的数学」（第 1 个义项：研究数与形及其关系的学问）；句意为她学了四年数学之后才转向经济学。图中可辨识物件：黑板、粉笔、算式、板槽；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 数学（学科名，形式为复数而作单数用）

senses.title: The discipline as a whole
senses.definition: the field of study that reasons about number, quantity, structure and shape
senses.definitionCN: 研究数、量、结构与形的学问领域
senses.example: She studied mathematics for four years before turning to economics.
senses.exampleCN: 她学了四年数学之后才转向经济学。
senses.why: The word names a whole discipline rather than one of its branches, so it is used with a singular verb despite its plural shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是整门学问而非某一分支，因此尽管外形是复数，却接单数动词。

senses.title: The school subject and its lessons
senses.definition: the subject taught in schools, together with the lessons and examinations that go with it
senses.definitionCN: 学校里教授的这一科目，以及随之而来的课程与考试
senses.example: Mathematics is timetabled before lunch three days a week.
senses.exampleCN: 数学课每周有三天排在午饭前。
senses.why: Once a discipline enters a timetable it becomes a subject, and the same word covers both the field and the hour it occupies.
senses.whyCN: 一门学问一旦进入课表就成了科目，同一个词既指这个领域，也指它占用的那一节课。

senses.title: Reckoning and reasoning in practice
senses.titleCN: 实际推算与推理的活动
senses.definition: the activity of calculating and reasoning with numbers in a particular situation
senses.definitionCN: 在具体情境中运用数字进行计算与推理的活动
senses.example: The mathematics behind the bridge design was checked twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥设计背后的数学计算被核对了两遍。
senses.why: Here the word means the working itself, not the science of it: the sums someone actually did.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词指实际运算本身，而不是关于运算的学问：某人真做过的那些计算。

senses.title: The mathematical side of a subject
senses.titleCN: 某一对象内部的数学机制
senses.definition: the quantitative structure and relationships that underlie a particular process or system
senses.definitionCN: 支撑某一过程或系统的数量结构与关系
senses.example: The mathematics of traffic flow decides where queues form.
senses.exampleCN: 车流的数学机制决定了排队会在哪里形成。
senses.why: Any system with regular quantities has a mathematics of its own, and the phrase names that structure rather than the discipline.
senses.whyCN: 任何具有规律数量的系统都有自己的数学，这个说法指那套结构，而非那门学科。

senses.title: The professional community
senses.definition: the community of people who work in the field, taken as a body
senses.definitionCN: 以整体看待的、从事这一领域的人所组成的群体
senses.example: The result was celebrated across mathematics before it was published.
senses.exampleCN: 这一结果在发表之前就已在数学界传开。
senses.why: A discipline also names its practitioners as a group, which is why one can speak of a whole field being excited.
senses.whyCN: 一门学问也指其从业者的群体，因此可以说整个领域为之振奋。

senses.title: Careful reckoning in plain speech
senses.definition: used informally for the calculating needed to make a decision come out right
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指为使某项决定算得过来所需的精密推算
senses.example: The mathematics of the deal did not survive the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔交易的账在新税之下算不过来了。
senses.why: Everyday speech borrows the discipline's name for the arithmetic of a practical decision.
senses.whyCN: 日常说法借这门学问之名，指一项实际决定背后的加减账。

senses.title: The old sense of learning
senses.definition: in its Greek origin, any branch of learning rather than the numerical sciences alone
senses.definitionCN: 在其希腊来源中泛指任何一门学问，而非仅指数理科学
senses.example: In the ancient curriculum, music and astronomy counted as mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 在古代课程里，音乐与天文也算作数学。
senses.why: The Greek word meant something learned, so the discipline once covered far more ground than it does now.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原词意为「被学到的东西」，因此这门学问早先涵盖的范围远大于今天。

senses.title: The mathematical content of a paper
senses.titleCN: 论文或模型中的数学内容
senses.definition: the equations, proofs and derivations contained in a piece of work
senses.definitionCN: 一项工作中所含的方程、证明与推导
senses.example: The biology paper was strong, but its mathematics was thin.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇生物学论文很强，但其中的数学部分薄弱。
senses.why: Readers separate a work's subject matter from its mathematical machinery, and this sense names the latter.
senses.whyCN: 读者会把一项工作的主题与其数学工具分开，这个义项指后者。

intro.en: The word goes back to Greek mathēma 'that which is learned', from manthanein 'to learn'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词可追溯到希腊语 mathēma「被学到的东西」，源自动词 manthanein「学习」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Manthanein meant 'to learn', and gave mathēma 'a lesson, something learned' and mathesis 'learning'. The deeper root is reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: manthanein 意为「学习」，由此得到 mathēma「课业、所学之物」与 mathesis「学习」。更深词根属重构形式，并无实证。

items.en: Mathēmatikos meant 'fond of learning, learned'; ta mathēmatika named the things studied rather than a single science.
items.cn: mathēmatikos 意为「爱学习的、有学问的」；中性复数形式指的是所学的那些东西，而非单一学科。

items.en: The phrase mathēmatikē tekhnē, 'the art of learning', was narrowed by Plato and Aristotle to arithmetic, geometry, astronomy and music.
items.cn: 「学习的技艺」这一短语经柏拉图与亚里士多德之手，收窄为算术、几何、天文与音乐四门。

items.en: Latin took mathematica as a name for that group of studies, and medieval schools taught them in the quadrivial curriculum.
items.cn: 拉丁语以 mathematica 作为这组学问之名，中世纪学校在四艺课程中教授它们。

items.en: English adopted the word in the sixteenth century; the plural form is treated as singular because it names one field.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收这个词；复数外形被当作单数使用，因为它命名的是一个领域。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the field expanded far beyond number and shape, and the old sense of any learning survives only in histories of the curriculum. First date uncertain: the earliest English citation is placed in the sixteenth century but no single year is agreed.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，该领域远远超出数与形，而「任何学问」的旧义只留在课程史中。首见年代不确定：最早英语书证被放在十六世纪，但没有公认的确切年份。

note.en: Group one separates forms of the same word that are easy to mix up; group two separates the neighbouring branches of the field.
note.cn: 第一组辨析同一个词的各种形式，第二组辨析相邻的学科分支。

entries.definition: An older singular and adjective form, now rare; modern English keeps the plural shape for the field and uses mathematical for the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 更早的单数形式与形容词形式，今已罕用；现代英语以复数外形指该领域，形容词则另用形式。

entries.definition: The adjective of the field; it describes work or reasoning rather than naming the discipline itself.
entries.definitionCN: 该领域的形容词；它描述工作或推理，而不命名学科本身。

entries.definition: The practitioner; the ending marks a person, which is the one clear difference from the field name.
entries.definitionCN: 指从业者；词尾标记出人，这是与学科名唯一清楚的差别。

entries.definition: A rare English borrowing of the Greek noun for learning, used in older philosophical writing; it never named the school subject.
entries.definitionCN: 英语直接从希腊语借入的罕见名词，意为学习，见于较早的哲学写作；它从未指学校科目。

entries.definition: The branch that handles counting and the four operations; it is a part of mathematics, not a synonym for it.
entries.definitionCN: 处理计数与四则运算的分支；它是数学的一部分，而不是数学的同义词。

entries.definition: The branch that works with symbols standing for unknown numbers; one department within the larger field.
entries.definitionCN: 用符号代表未知数进行运算的分支；是更大领域中的一个部门。

entries.definition: The branch that studies shape, size and the relations of figures in space.
entries.definitionCN: 研究形状、大小与空间中图形关系的分支。

entries.definition: The practical ability to handle numbers in daily life; it is a skill, whereas mathematics is a discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 在日常生活中处理数字的实际能力；它是一种技能，而数学是一门学问。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Greek root means 'that which is learned', so mathematics began as the name for any studied subject.
normal.cn: 希腊词根意为「被学到的东西」，因此数学最初泛指任何被研习的科目。

normal.en: The plural shape takes a singular verb: mathematics is one field, not many.
normal.cn: 复数外形接单数动词：数学是一个领域，而不是许多个。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the division of the field: pure mathematics, applied mathematics, advanced mathematics.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域的划分：纯数学、应用数学、高等数学。

normal.en: The family runs mathematics, mathematical, mathematician, mathematically, plus the clippings math and maths.
normal.cn: 同族词包括数学、数学的、数学家、在数学上，另有口语缩略形式。

normal.en: Ancient schooling grouped it with music and astronomy, so the old sense was wider than today's.
normal.cn: 古代课程把它与音乐、天文编在一起，因此旧义比今天宽。

abstract.en: Picture a single chalk line drawn again and again until it is unmistakably straight.
abstract.cn: 想象一条粉笔线被反复描画，直到直得无可置疑。

abstract.en: Picture a key ring that opens every locked door in a building, whatever the door was made for.
abstract.cn: 想象一串钥匙能打开楼里每一扇锁着的门，无论那扇门原本是做什么用的。

abstract.en: Picture a language spoken by few people but understood, in translation, by everyone.
abstract.cn: 想象一种只有少数人会说的语言，却人人能通过翻译读懂。

examples.en: Mathematics is compulsory for every student in the first two years.
examples.cn: 头两年每个学生都必须学数学。

examples.en: The mathematics of the model turned out to be simpler than expected.
examples.cn: 这个模型的数学部分比预想的简单。

examples.en: He teaches mathematics at a secondary school.
examples.cn: 他在一所中学教数学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「学来的东西」：希腊词根意为学习，凡学得的学问都算 → 数学

root: 希腊 mathēma「被学到的东西」源自动词 manthanein「学习」，mathēmatikē tekhnē 经柏拉图与亚里士多德收窄为四艺；拉丁 mathematica 承之，英语十六世纪借入，复数外形作单数用。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the discipline as a whole to its school hours, its practical working, the structure inside another subject, its professional community, plain-speech reckoning, the ancient sense of any learning, and the mathematics inside a single paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从作为整体的学科，移到它的课时、实际运算、另一对象内部的结构、专业共同体、口语里的算账、古代泛指学问的旧义，最后到一篇论文里的数学部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blackboard filled with lines of symbols, one equal sign pressed hard at the end.
core.cn: 核心意象：写满符号行的黑板，末尾一个被重重描过的等号。

branches.en: The field and its old name: what began as any studied subject became one discipline.
branches.cn: 领域与其旧名：最初泛指任何被研习的科目，后来成了一口学科。

branches.en: Where it is taught and where it is printed: a timetable hour and a thin section of a paper.
branches.cn: 教它的地方与印它的地方：课表上的一节，论文里薄弱的一节。

branches.en: Reckoning in practice: the sums behind a bridge or behind a deal.
branches.cn: 实际算账：桥背后的算式，或一笔交易背后的账。

branches.en: The hidden structure: every regular system carries a mathematics of its own.
branches.cn: 隐在的结构：每个有规律的系统都自带一套数学。

branches.en: The people: a field is also the body of those who work in it.
branches.cn: 人：一个领域也是从事者的群体。

intro.en: The English word is a Greek noun with a Greek suffix, filtered through Latin and given an English plural ending.
intro.cn: 这个英语词是一个希腊名词加希腊后缀，经拉丁语过滤，又换上英语复数词尾。

latinIntro.en: Greek mathēma and mathēmatikos supply the meaning; Latin mathematica fixed the school subject, and English added the plural -s.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语的名词与形容词提供意义；拉丁语固定了学科之名，英语再加复数词尾。

items.example: The root names learning before it names number.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根先指学习，后指数。

items.example: The verb stands at the head of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词位于整个词族的起点。

items.example: The suffix names a skilled practice, not a body of facts.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名一门技艺，而非一堆事实。

items.meaningCN: 有学问的；属于数学之物的
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词从「有学问的」转为「数理的」。

items.example: Latin fixed the plural shape that English inherited.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语固定了英语所继承的复数外形。

items.structure: English plural ending used for fields of study
items.example: The ending marks a discipline while keeping a plural look.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记一门学科，同时保留复数外形。

items.example: The word names one field with a plural form.
items.exampleCN: 这个词以复数形式命名一个领域。

items.example: The adjective serves whenever a noun follows.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词用于修饰后面的名词。

items.meaning: a person who works in the field
items.example: The person suffix completes the family.

latinEntries.structure: mathesis, mathesis (f., third declension, from Greek)

definition_en: to change slowly into a new form
core_image: 一颗种子在四季里长成开花的树
scene: 这株植物为了适应干旱，逐渐演化出更厚的叶片。 The plant evolved thicker leaves in order to survive the drought.
sceneCN: 这里 evolve 是「逐渐演化」（第 1 个义项：生物经过世代发展出新特征）；句意：这株植物为了适应干旱，逐渐演化出更厚的叶片。

senses.title: Biological change
senses.definition: to develop new features over generations
senses.definitionCN: 经过许多世代发展出新特征
senses.example: Birds evolved from small dinosaurs.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟类由小型恐龙进化而来。
senses.why: Evolvere means to unroll, as a species unfolds over time.
senses.whyCN: evolvere 意为展开，物种随时间展开。

senses.title: Gradual development
senses.definition: to develop slowly
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢地发展
senses.example: The plan evolved into a full project.
senses.exampleCN: 计划逐渐发展成一个完整项目。
senses.why: Any idea can unfold like a living form.
senses.whyCN: 任何想法都能像生命形态一样展开。

senses.title: To give off
senses.definition: to give off gas or heat
senses.definitionCN: 释放气体或热量
senses.example: The reaction evolved a sharp smell.
senses.exampleCN: 反应释放出刺鼻的气味。
senses.why: Unrolling can mean letting something out.
senses.whyCN: 展开也可以指让某物释放出来。

intro.en: Evolve comes from Latin evolvere, to unroll.
intro.cn: evolve 源自拉丁语 evolvere（展开）。

items.en: Volvere means to roll.
items.cn: volvere 意为滚。

items.en: Evolvere means to unroll.
items.cn: evolvere 意为展开。

items.en: Evolve first means to unfold.
items.cn: evolve 最初指展开。

items.en: It comes to mean slow biological change.
items.cn: 它逐渐指缓慢的生物变化。

items.en: It also means to develop gradually.
items.cn: 它也指逐渐发展。

note.en: Evolve is slow and natural; develop can be planned.
note.cn: evolve 是缓慢自然的；develop 可以是有计划的。

entries.definition: slow change over time
relating to evolution
able to evolve
to grow or change over time
to change to fit a new situation
to move toward a better state

normalIntro.en: Evolve is a seed slowly becoming a tree.
normalIntro.cn: evolve 是一颗种子慢慢长成树。

normal.en: Evolve from means come from an older form.
normal.cn: evolve from 意为从更早的形态发展而来。

normal.en: Evolve into means become something new.
normal.cn: evolve into 意为演变成新事物。

normal.en: Slowly evolve means change over a long time.
normal.cn: slowly evolve 意为经过很长时间变化。

normal.en: Evolve over time means develop gradually.
normal.cn: evolve over time 意为随时间逐渐发展。

normal.en: Compare develop: develop can be planned, evolve is usually natural.
normal.cn: 对比 develop：develop 可以计划，evolve 通常自然发生。

abstract.en: Picture a seed becoming a flowering tree through four seasons.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗种子在四季中长成开花的树。

abstract.en: Imagine a rough sketch slowly turning into a clear map.
abstract.cn: 想象粗糙草图慢慢变成清晰地图。

abstract.en: Think of a river that slowly finds a new path.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河慢慢找到新的河道。

examples.en: The company evolved from a small shop.
examples.cn: 这家公司由一家小店发展而来。

examples.en: Animals evolve to survive in new places.
examples.cn: 动物进化以适应新环境。

examples.en: Her style evolved over many years.
examples.cn: 她的风格经过许多年逐渐演变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（出）＋ volve（转）」——慢慢转出来、展开来，就是进化、发展。

root: 拉丁语 evolvere（展开）＝ e-（出）＋ volvere（滚）→ evolve，核心义「逐渐展开、演化」。

sensesIntro.en: Evolve begins with biological change, extends to gradual development, and keeps an older sense of giving off.
sensesIntro.cn: evolve 从生物变化开始，延伸到逐渐发展，还保留了释放的旧义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seed becoming a flowering tree through four seasons.
core.cn: 核心意象：种子在四季中长成开花的树。

branches.en: Species change is the core modern sense.
branches.cn: 物种变化是现代核心含义。

branches.en: Plans and styles can evolve too.
branches.cn: 计划与风格也能逐渐发展。

branches.en: The old sense is to give off.
branches.cn: 古老含义是释放。

branches.en: Nature and human plans both unfold.
branches.cn: 自然与人类计划都会展开。

branches.en: Unrolling underlies change and release.
branches.cn: 展开的意象支撑变化与释放。

intro.en: Evolve combines e-, out, with the Latin root volv, to roll.
intro.cn: evolve 由 e-（出）与拉丁词根 volv（滚）组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin evolvere is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 evolvere 是直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Evolvere is the direct Latin source.
latinEntries.exampleCN: evolvere 是直接拉丁语来源。

definition_zh: 公制的；度量的；格律的；度量指标
definition_en: based on the metric system; also relating to measurement or to poetic metre, and as a noun a measure used to judge performance
core_image: 一把带刻度的尺，把长度拆成一个个可以比较的数字
scene: 实验室的白板上列着两套单位，年轻的研究员把英制数字逐个换算成公制。 The intern turned every figure on the board into metric units.
sceneCN: 这里是「公制的」（第 1 个义项：使用公制单位计量）；句意为实习生把白板上的每个数字都换成了公制单位。图中可辨识物件：白板、粉笔、写满数字的表格。

derivatives.zh: 由 metric 加 -al 构成，义为「格律的；度量的」
由 metric 加 -ation 构成，义为「改用公制」
由 metrical 加 -ly 构成，义为「按公制地；按格律地」

senses.title: Relating to the metric system
senses.definition: using or based on the metric system, in which units such as the metre and the kilogram are used
senses.definitionCN: 使用或基于公制的，即以米、千克等单位计量
senses.example: The label lists the weight in metric units.
senses.exampleCN: 标签上用公制单位标注重量。
senses.why: The Greek root metron meant a measure, and after the French reform the adjective was attached to the system built on the metre, so metric labels anything counted in those units.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 metron 意为「尺度」，法国公制改革之后这个形容词被贴到以米为基础的那套单位上，凡是按这套单位计量的东西都叫 metric。

senses.title: A measurement used to judge performance
senses.definition: a measurement used to judge performance or progress, most often in the plural form metrics
senses.definitionCN: 用来衡量表现或进展的测量值，最常用复数形式 metrics
senses.example: The team reviews three metrics every Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 团队每周一复盘三项指标。
senses.why: If metron is any measure, then a single number taken from a process is also a metron, and business English turned that into the countable metrics of a dashboard.
senses.whyCN: 既然 metron 泛指任何一种度量，那么从流程里取出一个数字也是一种度量，商业英语便把它变成仪表盘上可数的 metrics。

senses.title: Of measurement in general
senses.definition: concerned with measuring distance, size or quantity rather than with the units of one particular system
senses.definitionCN: 与距离、大小或数量的测量有关，而不是特指某一套单位
senses.example: In a metric space, distance is defined by a rule rather than by a ruler.
senses.exampleCN: 在度量空间里，距离由一条规则定义，而不是用尺子量出。
senses.why: Mathematics kept the oldest sense of metron as sheer measure, so metric can describe any structure that allows a distance to be assigned, with no metres or inches involved.
senses.whyCN: 数学保留了 metron 最古老的「度量」本义，因此 metric 可以描述任何一种能给出距离的结构，与米或英寸都无关。

senses.title: Of poetic metre
senses.definition: relating to metre, the patterned rhythm of stressed and unstressed syllables in verse
senses.definitionCN: 与格律有关的，即诗句中轻重音节形成的节奏模式
senses.example: The critic counted the metric feet in each line.
senses.exampleCN: 评论者数了每一行里的格律音步。
senses.why: Greek metrikos described verse measured out in feet, and the same adjective survived in literary criticism long after it had been applied to weights and lengths.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 metrikos 本指按音步「量」出来的诗句，这个形容词在文学批评里一直保留，后来才被用到重量与长度上。

intro.en: Metric comes from a Greek word for measure, reached English through Latin and French, and split between the sense of a system of units and the sense of a numbered measure.
intro.cn: metric 出自希腊语中表示「度量」的词，经拉丁语与法语进入英语，并在「单位体系」与「可计量的数值」两个方向上都站稳了脚。

items.en: Metron was any measure or unit of length, and it also named the unit of rhythm in verse.
items.cn: metron 泛指任何尺度或长度单位，也指诗句中节奏的单位。

items.en: The adjective metrikos meant of measure and was used especially for the measured rhythm of poetry.
items.cn: 形容词 metrikos 意为「关于度量的」，尤用于诗句中被量出的节奏。

items.en: Late Latin borrowed the Greek adjective as metricus, keeping the literary and measuring senses together.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语借入这个希腊形容词写作 metricus，把文学与度量两层意思一并保留。

items.en: During the French reform of weights and measures, the word was fixed to the system based on the metre, and the phrase système métrique spread across Europe.
items.cn: 在法国度量衡改革中，这个词被固定到以米为基础的体系上，système métrique 这一说法传遍欧洲。

items.en: English took metric in the nineteenth century for the system of units, then reused it for any number a business tracks and for the older sense of verse rhythm.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪借入 metric 指单位体系，随后又用它指企业追踪的任何数值，并保留了诗律的旧义。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Greek measure root through metre, geometry and the derived adjective; the near-meaning group collects words for measuring and for standards of comparison.
note.cn: 形近组顺着希腊语「度量」词根，收 metre、geometry 与派生形容词；近义组收表示测量与比较标准的词。

entries.definition: The base unit of length in the metric system.
entries.definitionCN: 公制中长度的基本单位。

entries.definition: The American spelling of metre; also a device that measures.
entries.definitionCN: metre 的美式拼写；也指计量仪表。

entries.definition: Relating to poetic metre or to measurement.
The mathematics of shapes and distances, named from measuring the earth.
entries.definitionCN: 研究形状与距离的数学，名字来自「测量土地」。

entries.definition: The act or result of finding a size or amount.
entries.definitionCN: 测量行为或测量所得的结果。

entries.definition: A fixed amount used as a standard for measuring.
entries.definitionCN: 作为计量标准的固定量。

entries.definition: An instrument or standard used for measuring something.
A standard point of reference for judging performance.
entries.definitionCN: 评判表现所用的参照标准。

normalIntro.en: One Greek word for measure runs through units, geometry and verse, so the family looks scattered but keeps a single idea.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示「度量」的希腊词贯穿单位、几何与诗句，所以这一族看着分散，内核却只有一个。

normal.en: Metron is Greek for a measure, and metre is the measure the metric system starts from.
normal.cn: metron 是希腊语中的「尺度」，metre 正是公制起步的那把尺。

normal.en: Metric as an adjective belongs to the system, which is why metric system and metric unit appear as fixed pairs.
normal.cn: 作形容词的 metric 依附于这套体系，所以 metric system 与 metric unit 是固定搭配。

normal.en: Metrics, the plural noun, turns one measurement into the set of numbers a dashboard watches.
normal.cn: 复数名词 metrics 把一次测量变成仪表盘上盯着的一组数字。

normal.en: Geometry ends in the same Greek word, so its name literally means measuring the land.
normal.cn: geometry 的词尾是同一个希腊词，名字字面上就是「测量土地」。

normal.en: Metrical keeps the verse sense, because Greek metre also counted the feet of a line.
normal.cn: metrical 保留了诗句的义项，因为希腊语的 metre 也用来数一行诗的音步。

abstract.en: A ruler and a dashboard do the same thing: they turn the world into numbers someone can compare.
abstract.cn: 尺子和仪表盘做的是同一件事：把世界变成可以互相比较的数字。

abstract.en: The word sits between a poem and a machine, measuring both a line of verse and a sack of grain.
abstract.cn: 这个词站在诗与机器之间，既量一行诗，也称一袋粮食。

abstract.en: Choosing what to count is choosing what matters, so a metric is never a neutral number.
abstract.cn: 决定数什么，就是决定在意什么，所以指标从来不是中立的数字。

examples.en: The form asks for your height in metric units.
examples.cn: 表格要求用公制单位填写身高。

examples.en: We track two metrics: response time and error rate.
examples.cn: 我们跟踪两项指标：响应时间和错误率。

examples.en: The poet kept a strict metric pattern in every line.
examples.cn: 这位诗人在每一行都保持严格的格律。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米特里克」——头一个字就是米，公制从米量起；记住 metric 是公制的，也指度量指标。

root: 希腊语 metron（尺度）派生 metrikos（关于度量的），经晚期拉丁语 metricus 与法语 métrique 进入英语；同族词包括 metre 与 geometry。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the act of measuring; the senses divide into a system of units, a countable number on a dashboard, measurement in general, and the measured rhythm of verse.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「度量」这个动作；义项分到单位体系、仪表盘上的可数数值、一般意义的测量，以及被量出节奏的诗句。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler with fine marks, turning length into numbers that can be compared.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把刻着细密刻度的尺，把长度变成可以互相比较的数字。

branches.en: a cookbook printing grams beside ounces
branches.cn: 食谱上把克与盎司并排印出

branches.en: a dashboard with three numbers on it
branches.cn: 仪表盘上只挂着三个数字

branches.en: a map where distance comes from a rule, not a ruler
branches.cn: 地图上的距离由规则给出，而不是用尺量

branches.en: a line of verse scanned for its beat
branches.cn: 一行诗被数出它的节拍

branches.en: the same act of measuring, once in units and once in numbers
branches.cn: 同一个测量动作，一次落在单位上，一次落在数字上

intro.en: Greek measure and its adjective supply the stem, and English suffixes and the geometry compound carry the family in several directions.
intro.cn: 希腊语的「度量」名词与形容词提供词干，再由英语后缀与 geometry 这个复合词把词族引向几个方向。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_en: relating to atoms, or using the energy released from them
core_image: 墙上钉着一张电子绕核的模型图
scene: 实验室门口贴着辐射警示标志。 The lab handles atomic materials with great care.
sceneCN: 这里 atomic 是「原子的」（第 1 个义项：与原子有关的）；句意是实验室非常小心地处理原子材料。

pos.zh: 形容词：原子的；原子能的

senses.title: Relating to atoms
senses.definition: relating to atoms or their structure
senses.definitionCN: 与原子本身或其结构有关
senses.example: The lab handles atomic materials with great care.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室非常小心地处理原子材料。
senses.why: Atomic is atom plus -ic, a suffix meaning 'relating to', so it describes whatever belongs to the study or structure of atoms.
senses.whyCN: atomic 是 atom 加 -ic，这个后缀表示「与……有关」，所以它形容一切属于原子研究或原子结构的事物。

senses.title: Using nuclear energy
senses.definition: using the energy released when atomic nuclei are split or joined
senses.definitionCN: 利用原子核裂变或聚变释放的能量
senses.example: Atomic power plants supply electricity to the region.
senses.exampleCN: 核电站为这一地区供电。
senses.why: Because the first large-scale use of this energy was described as atomic, the adjective widened from the particle to the power released from it.
senses.whyCN: 由于这种能量最早被大规模使用时称作原子能，形容词就从「原子本身」扩大到「原子释放出的动力」。

intro.en: Atomic is a scientific adjective built on the Greek word for an uncut particle.
intro.cn: atomic 是建立在希腊语「不可切分的微粒」之上的科学形容词。

items.en: atomos meant 'indivisible'.
items.cn: atomos 意为「不可分割的」。

items.en: atomus named the smallest particle.
items.cn: atomus 指最小微粒。

items.en: Atom entered English as the basic unit of matter.
items.cn: atom 作为物质基本单位进入英语。

items.en: Atomic was formed to mean 'of atoms'.
items.cn: atomic 被构成，意为「原子的」。

items.en: Atomic extended to nuclear energy and weapons.
items.cn: atomic 扩展到核能与核武器领域。

note.en: The look-alike group is the atom family; the near-meaning group gives scientific adjectives.
note.cn: 形近组是 atom 词族；近义组是其他科学形容词。

entries.definition: the smallest particle
to spray into fine drops
the theory of atoms
relating to atomic nuclei
relating to molecules
too small to see

normalIntro.en: Atomic describes the particle first and the power it releases second.
normalIntro.cn: atomic 先说微粒本身，再说由它释放的动力。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-TOM-ic.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

normal.en: The noun is atom, the adjective adds -ic.
normal.cn: 名词是 atom，形容词加 -ic。

normal.en: For energy, atomic and nuclear are close in meaning.
normal.cn: 指能源时，atomic 与 nuclear 含义接近。

normal.en: Atomic number names the count of protons.
normal.cn: atomic number 指质子数。

normal.en: Do not write atomical in modern English.
normal.cn: 现代英语不写 atomical。

abstract.en: See a diagram of rings around one dot.
abstract.cn: 想象一个点外围着几圈轨道。

abstract.en: See a warning sign with three blades on a door.
abstract.cn: 想象门上贴着三叶形的警示标志。

abstract.en: See a single lamp lit by a distant plant.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯由远处电厂点亮。

examples.en: The lab handles atomic materials with great care.
examples.cn: 实验室非常小心地处理原子材料。

examples.en: Atomic power plants supply electricity to the region.
examples.cn: 核电站为这一地区供电。

examples.en: The atomic number of carbon is six.
examples.cn: 碳的原子序数是六。

dict_mnemonic.text: atom（原子）加 -ic（与……有关）：与原子结构有关的，是原子的；由原子核释放的能量，是原子能。

root: 由 atom 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成；atom 源自希腊语 atomos「不可分割的」，因此 atomic 本指「与原子有关的」，二十世纪又扩展到核能领域。

sensesIntro.en: The particle and the power inside it are described by one adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: 微粒本身与它内部的能量，共用一个形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dot with rings drawn around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个点，外围画着轨道。

branches.en: atomic structure
branches.cn: 原子结构

branches.en: atomic number
branches.cn: 原子序数

branches.en: atomic materials
branches.cn: 原子材料

branches.en: atomic energy
branches.cn: 原子能

branches.en: atomic power
branches.cn: 核动力

intro.en: The adjective uses the -ic ending, as in basic and organic.
intro.cn: 这个形容词用 -ic 结尾，与 basic、organic 相同。

latinIntro.en: Atom itself came from Greek through Latin, and the -ic ending is Latin too.
latinIntro.cn: atom 经拉丁语转来，-ic 这个结尾同样来自拉丁语。

definition_en: to make someone feel annoyed or to prevent a plan from succeeding
core_image: 年轻的工程师对着失败的实验装置叹气
scene: 一次又一次的失败让这位年轻的工程师感到挫败。 Repeated failures frustrated the young engineer.
sceneCN: 这里 frustrate 是「使感到挫败」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一次又一次的失败让这位年轻的工程师感到挫败。

senses.title: Make someone feel blocked
senses.definition: to make someone feel annoyed because they cannot succeed
senses.definitionCN: 使人因无法成功而感到恼火
senses.example: Repeated failures frustrated the young engineer.
senses.exampleCN: 一次又一次的失败让这位年轻的工程师感到挫败。
senses.why: This is the feeling sense most learners meet first.
senses.whyCN: 这是学习者最先接触的情绪义项。

senses.title: Block a plan
senses.definition: to prevent a plan or effort from succeeding
senses.definitionCN: 阻止计划或努力取得成功
senses.example: Bad weather frustrated their plans for a picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 坏天气打乱了他们野餐的计划。
senses.why: Here the object is a plan, not a person.
senses.whyCN: 这里宾语是计划，而不是人。

senses.title: Make hopes fail
senses.definition: to make someone's hopes or expectations fail
senses.definitionCN: 使某人的希望或期待落空
senses.example: The long delay frustrated her hopes of winning.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的延误使她获胜的希望落空。
senses.why: Hopes can be blocked just like plans.
senses.whyCN: 希望也会像计划一样被阻挠。

intro.en: Frustrate goes back to a Latin word for vain effort.
intro.cn: frustrate 可追溯到拉丁语中表示徒劳的词。

items.en: Frustra meant in vain.
items.cn: frustra 意为徒劳。

items.en: Frustrari meant to deceive or disappoint.
items.cn: frustrari 意为欺骗或使失望。

items.en: Frustratus became its past participle.
items.cn: frustratus 成为它的过去分词。

items.en: The verb entered English as frustrate.
items.cn: 这个动词以 frustrate 进入英语。

items.en: It now covers feelings, plans, and hopes.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖情绪、计划和希望。

note.en: Frustrate is compared with look-alike words and words for blocking.
note.cn: 把 frustrate 与形近词以及表示阻挠的词作比较。

a cone with the top cut off

normalIntro.en: Frustrate is the wall between effort and success.
normalIntro.cn: frustrate 是努力与成功之间的那堵墙。

normal.en: Repeated failures frustrated the young engineer.
normal.cn: 一次又一次的失败让年轻的工程师感到挫败。

normal.en: Bad weather frustrated their plans for a picnic.
normal.cn: 坏天气打乱了他们野餐的计划。

normal.en: The long delay frustrated her hopes of winning.
normal.cn: 漫长的延误使她获胜的希望落空。

normal.en: Slow traffic frustrates drivers every morning.
normal.cn: 缓慢的交通每天早晨都让司机沮丧。

normal.en: He felt frustrated by the endless rules.
normal.cn: 他被没完没了的规则弄得灰心。

abstract.en: Frustration is energy that has found no door.
abstract.cn: 挫败感是找不到出口的能量。

abstract.en: A blocked plan can teach a better route.
abstract.cn: 被阻挠的计划能教人找到更好的路线。

abstract.en: What frustrates us today may sharpen us tomorrow.
abstract.cn: 今天让我们受挫的事，明天也许让我们更锋利。

examples.cn: 一次又一次的失败让年轻的工程师感到挫败。

examples.en: Bad weather frustrated their plans for a picnic.

dict_mnemonic.text: frustrate 与 illustrate 形近，注意前缀不同；frustration 是「挫败感」，frustrating 是「令人沮丧的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 frustrari（使失望、使徒劳），词根 frustra 意为「徒劳」；核心义「使努力落空」。

sensesIntro.en: Frustrate covers making people annoyed, blocking plans, and dashing hopes.
sensesIntro.cn: frustrate 涵盖使人恼火、阻挠计划以及使希望落空。

core.en: Effort meets a wall and cannot pass.
core.cn: 努力撞上一堵墙，无法通过。

branches.en: A person feels stuck and annoyed.
branches.cn: 一个人感到受阻而恼火。

branches.en: A plan meets an obstacle.
branches.cn: 计划遇到障碍。

branches.en: A hope fades before it is reached.
branches.cn: 希望在到达之前消退。

branches.en: Blocked plans produce blocked feelings.
branches.cn: 受阻的计划产生受阻的情绪。

branches.en: Plans and hopes fail in the same way.
branches.cn: 计划与希望以同样的方式失败。

intro.en: Frustrate forms words about blocked effort and its feelings.
intro.cn: frustrate 构成一族表示受阻努力及其情绪的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base frustr- means in vain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 frustr- 意为徒劳。

items.example: The noise frustrates the whole class.
She looked frustrated after the test.

雨水使他们的努力受挫。

items.example: The strike frustrated our travel plans.
