items.example: Losing the file was a frustrating experience.
items.exampleCN: 丢失文件是一段令人沮丧的经历。

definition_zh: 腰；腰部；（衣服的）腰身；腰围
definition_en: the part of the body between the ribs and the hips, or the part of a garment that fits around it
core_image: 两手叉在身体中段，那里最窄也最能弯
scene: 裁缝绕着她的腰量了一圈，把数字写在纸样边上。 The coat was taken in at the waist so that it fitted better.
sceneCN: 这里 waist 是「腰部」（第 1 个义项：肋骨与胯之间的身体部分）；句意为大衣在腰部收窄，以便更合身。两手叉腰的那处身体中段，就是这个词的形象。

derivatives.zh: waist 与 coat 复合，义为「马甲」
waist 与 band 复合，义为「腰带；裤腰」
waist 与 line 复合，义为「腰线；腰围」
加 -ed 构成，常与形容词连用，如 high-waisted「高腰的」

senses.title: The middle of the body
senses.definition: the narrow middle part of the body between the chest and the hips
senses.definitionCN: 身体在胸与胯之间较窄的中段
senses.example: The coat was taken in at the waist so that it fitted better.
senses.exampleCN: 大衣在腰部收窄，以便更合身。
senses.why: The old word meant growth, then the place where a body grows and bends; the middle of the trunk took the name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的旧义是「生长」，随后指身体生长弯曲之处，躯干的中段便得了这个名字。

senses.title: The part of a garment there
senses.definition: the part of a dress, skirt or trousers that sits around the waist
senses.definitionCN: 裙、裤等衣服围绕腰部的那一部分
senses.example: The skirt has a wide waist with a hidden zip.
senses.exampleCN: 这条裙子腰身宽松，还藏着一个拉链。
senses.why: A garment copies the body it covers, so the middle seam of a dress is simply called the waist.
senses.whyCN: 衣服照抄它所包住的身体，裙子的中段接缝就被直接称为 waist。

senses.title: The measurement around it
senses.definition: the measurement of the body at that narrow point
senses.definitionCN: 在身体最窄处量出的周长
senses.example: His waist has not changed in twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他的腰围二十年没有变化。
senses.why: A size is quoted as the measurement of a part, so clothes are sold by waist as well as by chest.
senses.whyCN: 尺码常以某部位的测量值表示，所以衣服既按胸围也按腰围出售。

senses.title: The narrow middle of a thing
senses.definition: the narrower middle of a ship, an object or a shape
senses.definitionCN: 船体、器物或形状较窄的中段
senses.example: The ship was struck just forward of the waist.
senses.exampleCN: 船在腰段稍前处被击中。
senses.why: Any long body that swells at the ends and narrows in the middle can borrow the name of the human waist.
senses.whyCN: 任何两端粗、中间窄的长形物都可借用人腰的名字。

senses.title: The middle section of a violin family
senses.definition: the inward-curved middle of the body of a violin or a guitar
senses.definitionCN: 小提琴或吉他琴身向内收的中段
senses.example: The maker cut the waist of the instrument by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 制琴师手工把琴身的中腰挖出来。
senses.why: Instrument makers named the curved middle after the body, because the curve lets the bow move freely across the strings.
senses.whyCN: 制琴师按人体给这个弯中段命名，因为这段弯曲让弓能自由过弦。

intro.en: Waist goes back to a Germanic word for growth, which then named the growing middle of the body.
intro.cn: waist 上溯到日耳曼语表示「生长」的词，随后指身体生长、弯折的中段。

items.en: The root meant to grow, and the noun meant growth or increase.
items.cn: 词根意为生长，名词义为生长、增加。

items.en: Old English wæstm is recorded meaning growth, a fruit or a produce.
items.cn: 古英语 wæstm 有记录，义为生长、果实或收成。

items.en: The sense narrowed to the body's growing part, then to the narrow middle between ribs and hips.
items.cn: 词义缩到身体的生长部位，再缩到肋骨与胯之间的窄中段。

items.en: Tailoring took it over for the fitting part of a garment and for the size sold by it.
items.cn: 裁缝业借它指衣服合身的那一段，以及据它出售的尺码。

items.en: Shipbuilders and violin makers extended it to the narrow middle of what they make.
items.cn: 造船与制琴把它扩展到所造之物较窄的中段。

note.en: The first group follows the family and a common homophone, the second the neighbouring words for the body and for clothes.
note.cn: 第一组收同族词与常见同音词，第二组收身体与衣着的邻近词。

entries.definition: The plural of the noun.
A different word meaning loss or rubbish, with the same sound.
entries.definitionCN: 同音异义词，义为浪费、废物。

entries.definition: The band of cloth around the top of trousers.
The line of the waist, and the measurement at it.
The joint beside and below the waist.
The front of the body between chest and waist.
entries.definitionCN: 胸与腰之间的腹部前面。

entries.definition: The strap worn around the waist.
The trunk of the body, of which the waist is the narrow part.
entries.definitionCN: 躯干，腰是其中较窄的一段。

normalIntro.en: One short word, four long compounds, and one homophone to keep apart.
normalIntro.cn: 一个短词、四个复合词，以及一个必须分开的同音词。

normal.en: Waste and waist sound alike but waste is loss, waist is the body.
normal.cn: waste 与 waist 同音，但 waste 是浪费，waist 是身体部位。

normal.en: Compounds keep the spelling: waistcoat, waistband, waistline.
normal.cn: 复合词保留拼写：waistcoat、waistband、waistline。

normal.en: A waistcoat is a garment at the waist, a vest in American use.
normal.cn: waistcoat 是穿在腰部的衣物，美式称 vest。

normal.en: Tailored clothes are taken in at the waist.
normal.cn: 定制的衣服在腰部收窄。

normal.en: A violin has a waist because its sides curve inwards.
normal.cn: 小提琴有腰身，因为两侧向内弯。

abstract.en: Picture hands on the narrowest part of the body.
abstract.cn: 想两只手叉在身体最窄处。

abstract.en: See a ribbon tied around the middle of a parcel.
abstract.cn: 想一条丝带扎在包裹的中段。

abstract.en: Feel the inward curve of a guitar against your knee.
abstract.cn: 感受吉他的内弯贴在膝上。

examples.en: She tied the apron around her waist.
examples.cn: 她把围裙系在腰上。

examples.en: The water came up to his waist.
examples.cn: 水没到他的腰部。

examples.en: This dress is loose at the waist.
examples.cn: 这条裙子腰部较松。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「围丝」——用丝带围在腰上的那圈，就是腰部。

root: 日耳曼语 *wahs-（生长）→ 古英语 wæstm（生长、果实）→ 中古英语 waist（身体中段）→ 现代英语 waist。

sensesIntro.en: Growth narrows into the middle of the body, then spreads out again into clothes, sizes, ships and violins.
sensesIntro.cn: 「生长」先缩成身体中段，再向外铺开成衣服、尺码、船体与提琴的腰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands on the narrow middle of the body.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手叉在身体较窄的中段。

branches.en: The body branch: a coat taken in at the waist.
branches.cn: 身体分支：腰部收窄的大衣。

branches.en: The clothing branch: a skirt with a wide waist.
branches.cn: 衣着分支：腰身宽松的裙子。

branches.en: The size branch: a waist unchanged for twenty years.
branches.cn: 尺码分支：二十年不变的腰围。

branches.en: The object branch: the waist of a ship.
branches.cn: 器物分支：船的中腰。

branches.en: The instrument branch: the curved waist of a violin.
branches.cn: 乐器分支：小提琴内弯的中腰。

intro.en: Waist- already carries the body meaning; the compounds add coat, band, line and a past ending.
intro.cn: waist- 本身已带身体义，复合词再加 coat、band、line 与过去式词尾。

latinIntro.en: This root is Germanic; it has no Latin ancestor, so the entry lists no Latin word.
latinIntro.cn: 该词根为日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先，故不列拉丁词条。

items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族的基底。

items.example: It forms strip to the waist.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 strip to the waist。

items.example: Waste is a different word entirely.

definition_zh: 志愿者；志愿兵；自告奋勇者；自愿做；主动提供
definition_en: a person who freely offers to do something, especially without payment, or to offer oneself for a task
core_image: 人群中有人举起手，自己往前迈一步
scene: 洪水过后，社区大厅贴出招募告示，不到半天就挤满了人。 Dozens of volunteers arrived with shovels before the rain stopped.
sceneCN: 这里 volunteer 是「志愿者」（第 1 个义项：自愿不计报酬做事的人）；句意为雨还没停，几十名志愿者就带着铁锹赶到了。人群中有人举手往前迈的那一步，正是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 志愿者；志愿兵；自告奋勇者
自愿做；主动提供；自愿参军

collocations.zh: 自告奋勇承担这项任务

derivatives.zh: 同根形容词，义为「自愿的；无偿的」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「志愿服务；志愿活动」

senses.title: A person who offers to help
senses.definition: a person who offers to do something useful without being paid or forced
senses.definitionCN: 自愿不计报酬、也非被迫去做有益之事的人
senses.example: Dozens of volunteers arrived with shovels before the rain stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 雨还没停，几十名志愿者就带着铁锹赶到了。
senses.why: The noun comes from Latin voluntas, the will; a volunteer is someone whose coming depends on nothing but the will.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自拉丁语 voluntas（意志），volunteer 就是来与不来只看意志的人。

senses.title: To offer oneself for a task
senses.definition: to say that one is willing to do something, before being asked
senses.definitionCN: 在被要求之前就表示愿意去做
senses.example: She volunteered to drive the injured man to the clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 她自告奋勇开车送伤者去诊所。
senses.why: The verb turns the person into the action: stepping forward before anyone calls your name.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「人」变成「动作」：在有人点你的名字之前就跨前一步。

senses.title: To give information without being asked
senses.definition: to offer a remark or a piece of information freely, without a question
senses.definitionCN: 不经询问就主动说出看法或信息
senses.example: He volunteered a detail that the police had not asked about.
senses.exampleCN: 他主动说出一个警方并未问到的细节。
senses.why: Anything given without a request follows the same pattern: it is offered by the will, not pulled out by a question.
senses.whyCN: 凡未经请求就给出的东西都遵循同一模式：由意志主动给出，而非被问题拽出来。

senses.title: A soldier who serves by choice
senses.definition: a person who joins the armed forces by choice rather than by conscription
senses.definitionCN: 自愿入伍而非被征召的军人
senses.example: He served as a volunteer for three years before the war ended.
senses.exampleCN: 战争结束前他当了三年志愿兵。
senses.why: Armies once filled their ranks by force; a soldier who came freely stood out and took the same name as the helper.
senses.whyCN: 军队曾靠强制填补兵员，自愿前来的士兵格外显眼，于是与帮忙的人共用同一个名字。

senses.title: A plant growing without being sown
senses.definition: a plant that grows on its own from seed dropped by other plants
senses.definitionCN: 由别的植物落下的种子自己长出来的植物
senses.example: A volunteer appeared among the wheat and was left to grow.
senses.exampleCN: 麦田里冒出一株自生植物，被留着生长。
senses.why: Botany took the word for anything that arrives by itself, not planted by a hand.
senses.whyCN: 植物学借这个词指自己到来、并非人手栽种的东西。

intro.en: Volunteer came through French from Latin voluntarius, an adjective built on voluntas, the will.
intro.cn: volunteer 经法语来自拉丁语 voluntarius，这个形容词建立在 voluntas（意志）上。

items.en: Velle meant to wish, and voluntas named the will; voluntarius described what was done freely.
items.cn: velle 意为愿意，voluntas 指意志，voluntarius 形容自由做成的事。

items.en: French volunteer was first a soldier who offered to serve, and the military sense came first.
items.cn: 法语 volunte 原指自愿服役的士兵，军事义先出现。

items.en: English borrowed it in the sixteen hundreds for anyone who offered service.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入该词，泛指任何主动提供服务的人。

items.en: The verb followed the noun, first as to enlist and later as to offer anything freely.
items.cn: 动词随后跟上，先指自愿入伍，后指主动给出任何东西。

items.en: Modern gardening and botany added the plant that grows by itself.
items.cn: 现代园艺与植物学又添上自己长出来的植物义。

note.en: The first group holds the will family, the second the words for helpers and for service given.
note.cn: 第一组收「意志」词族，第二组收帮手与提供服务一类词。

entries.definition: The plural of the noun and the third person of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数，也是动词三单。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning done by free choice.
The adverb, meaning of one's own will.
The activity of giving unpaid service.
A person who helps; says nothing about being paid.
A trainee gaining experience, sometimes unpaid but not voluntary.
entries.definitionCN: 实习者，有时不取酬但并非志愿性质。

entries.definition: Someone drawn in to join a force or a team.
entries.definitionCN: 被招募加入部队或团队的人。

entries.definition: A soldier forced to serve, the opposite of a volunteer.
entries.definitionCN: 被强征服役的士兵，与志愿兵相对。

normalIntro.en: The root is the will; the endings -eer and -ing just tell you who and what.
normalIntro.cn: 词根是「意志」，后缀 -eer 与 -ing 只说明是谁、是什么。

normal.en: Volunteer and voluntary share Latin voluntas, the will.
normal.cn: volunteer 与 voluntary 共享拉丁语 voluntas（意志）。

normal.en: The -eer ending names a person, as in engineer and mountaineer.
normal.cn: -eer 后缀指人，如 engineer、mountaineer。

normal.en: As a verb it takes an infinitive: volunteer to help.
normal.cn: 作动词时后接不定式：volunteer to help。

normal.en: A volunteer is not paid, but not every unpaid worker is a volunteer.
normal.cn: 志愿者不取报酬，但并非所有不取报酬的人都是志愿者。

normal.en: The plural volunteers does double duty for noun and verb.
normal.cn: 复数 volunteers 同时用作名词复数与动词三单。

abstract.en: See a hand go up in a crowd before anyone calls a name.
abstract.cn: 想人群中还没人点名，一只手已经举起。

abstract.en: Feel the one step forward that nobody ordered.
abstract.cn: 感受那一步没人命令却自己迈出的向前。

abstract.en: Picture a high-visibility vest with no name tag, only a willingness.
abstract.cn: 想一件没有名牌的高亮背心，只写着「愿意」。

examples.en: Each volunteer was given a map and a bottle of water.
examples.cn: 每位志愿者都领到一张地图和一瓶水。

examples.en: Nobody asked him, but he volunteered to carry the boxes.
examples.cn: 没人叫他，他却主动去搬箱子。

examples.en: The school needs volunteers to read with young children.
examples.cn: 学校需要志愿者陪小朋友读书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我愿提尔」——我愿提着尔的东西跑一趟，这就是志愿者。

root: 拉丁语 velle（愿意）→ voluntas（意志）→ 中世纪拉丁语 voluntarius → 法语 volunte（自愿入伍者）→ 英语 volunteer。

sensesIntro.en: The will becomes a person, then an action, then any freely given remark, then a freely enlisted soldier, then a plant that plants itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 意志先变成一个人，再变成一个动作、一句主动说出的话、一名自愿入伍的兵，最后一株自己长出来的植物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raised before anyone asks.
core.cn: 核心意象：还没人开口就举起的手。

branches.en: The person branch: people with shovels in the rain.
branches.cn: 人物分支：雨中拿铁锹的人们。

branches.en: The action branch: volunteering to drive someone to a clinic.
branches.cn: 动作分支：主动开车送人去诊所。

branches.en: The remark branch: a detail nobody asked for.
branches.cn: 言语分支：没人问就说出一个细节。

branches.en: The army branch: three years of free service.
branches.cn: 军队分支：三年自愿服役。

branches.en: The plant branch: a stalk among the wheat.
branches.cn: 植物分支：麦田里的那一株。

intro.en: Volunt- is the will, -eer names a person, and -ing turns the verb into an activity.
intro.cn: volunt- 是「意志」，-eer 指人，-ing 把动词变成活动。

latinIntro.en: Latin voluntas and voluntarius are recorded, and French volunte stands between them and the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 voluntas 与 voluntarius 均有记录，法语 volunte 夹在它们与英语词之间。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根携带「自由选择」之义。
它构成 volunteer 与 engineer。

items.meaning: more than one, or he does

items.example: It forms conscript, the opposite idea.
items.exampleCN: 它与 scribe 构成 conscript，表示相反的意思。

items.example: It forms recruit, a related word.
items.exampleCN: 它与 cruit 构成相关的 recruit。

items.example: A volunteer does what shall never forced.
items.exampleCN: 志愿者做的是从未被强求的事。

definition_zh: 继承（财产、地位或特征）；接手（遗留的问题）
definition_en: to receive money, property, or qualities from someone who has died or come before you
core_image: 老人留下的钥匙和账簿被交到下一代手里
scene: 祖父去世后，律师在书房里宣读遗嘱。 She inherited the old farmhouse and all the land around it.
sceneCN: 这里 inherit 是「继承财产」（第 1 个义项：从去世的人那里接受钱财或产业）；句意为她继承了那座旧农舍以及周围所有土地。图中可辨识物件：遗嘱、钥匙、旧账簿。

pos.zh: 动词：继承；接手；遗传获得

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「遗产；继承」
由本词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「继承人」
由本词加后缀构成，义为「可继承的」
由本词加否定前缀构成，义为「剥夺继承权」

senses.title: To receive property from the dead
senses.definition: to receive money, property, or a title from someone after that person has died
senses.definitionCN: 在某人身故后接受其钱财、产业或头衔
senses.example: She inherited the house from her aunt.
senses.exampleCN: 她从姑妈那里继承了这所房子。
senses.why: In- "in" plus heres "heir" gave inhereditare, to put someone in the position of an heir.
senses.whyCN: in-「进入」加 heres「继承人」构成 inhereditare，意为把人放进继承人的位置。

senses.title: To take over a legacy of problems
senses.definition: to receive a situation, problem, or duty that someone else has left behind
senses.definitionCN: 接受别人留下的局面、问题或职责
senses.example: The new mayor inherited a city deep in debt.
senses.exampleCN: 新市长接手了一座负债累累的城市。
senses.why: What is passed down is not always wealth; an office or a mess can be handed over in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 传下来的不总是财富；职位或一团乱局也能以同样的方式移交。

senses.title: To get a quality through genes
senses.definition: to receive a physical or personal quality from one's parents or ancestors through genes
senses.definitionCN: 通过基因从父母或祖先那里获得身体或性格特征
senses.example: He inherited his mother's quick temper.
senses.exampleCN: 他遗传了母亲的急性子。
senses.why: Biology borrowed the legal image: parents hand down traits as families hand down land.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了法律上的意象：父母传下特征，正如家族传下土地。

intro.en: Inherit is a legal Latin word whose heir has become the everyday word for anything handed down.
intro.cn: inherit 本是一个法律拉丁词，其中的「继承人」如今成了泛指一切传承的日常语汇。

items.en: Heres meant "heir", a person who steps into another's property and standing.
items.cn: heres 意为「继承人」，指接替他人财产与地位的人。

items.en: Inhereditare, "to make an heir", built in- onto heres and was used of transferring an estate.
items.cn: inhereditare 意为「使成为继承人」，由 in- 加 heres 构成，用于转移产业。

items.en: Old French enheriter, "to make heir, to put in possession", shortened the form on its way to English.
items.cn: 古法语 enheriter 意为「立为继承人、使其占有」，在传入英语时形式缩短。

items.en: English took inherit in the fourteenth century, first in law, then in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪引入 inherit，先用于法律，后进入日常语言。

items.en: Since the nineteenth century it also covers traits passed through genes, not just property.
items.cn: 十九世纪以后，它也涵盖经基因传下的特征，而不只是财产。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the heir root; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of receiving from someone else.
note.cn: 形近组保留「继承人」词根；近义组收其他表示「从他人处获得」的动词。

entries.definition: What is inherited, whether money or a trait.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「遗产、遗传」，指被继承之物。

entries.definition: The person who inherits property or a title.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「继承人」，即继承财产或头衔的人。

entries.definition: The traditions and buildings a society passes down.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「遗产、传统」，指社会传下的传统与建筑。

entries.definition: To take over an office or title after another person.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「继任」，多指接替职位或头衔。

entries.definition: To get something given to you, without the idea of a death.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「收到」，不含继承的意味。

entries.definition: To gain something by your own effort or purchase.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「获得」，强调靠自己努力或购买。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real heir root and the phrases the word actually takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的「继承人」词根，以及这个词实际使用的搭配。

normal.en: Heres is heir: to inherit is to be put in the heir's place.
normal.cn: heres 就是「继承人」：inherit 就是被放进继承人位置。

normal.en: The same root gives heir, heritage and inheritance.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 heir、heritage、inheritance。

normal.en: You inherit money from a person, but you inherit a problem from a situation.
normal.cn: 钱是从人那里 inherit 来的，问题是从局面那里 inherit 来的。

normal.en: An inherited disease comes through the genes, not through a will.
normal.cn: inherited disease 是通过基因而非遗嘱得来的。

normal.en: A new manager often inherits the mistakes of the old one.
normal.cn: 新经理常常要接手前任犯下的错误。

abstract.en: Picture a key passed from an old hand to a young one: the door opens for the new owner.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙从老人的手交到年轻人的手里：门为新主人打开。

abstract.en: Inheritance is time travelling forward: the past arrives in the present as property, habit or illness.
abstract.cn: 继承是时间向前旅行：过去以财产、习惯或疾病的形式抵达现在。

abstract.en: You choose what to keep and what to change, but you cannot choose what you were handed.
abstract.cn: 你可以选择保留什么、改变什么，却无法选择自己被交到手里的东西。

examples.en: He inherited a small workshop from his father.
examples.cn: 他从父亲那里继承了一间小作坊。

examples.en: Children often inherit the habits of their parents.
examples.cn: 孩子常会遗传父母的习惯。

examples.en: The committee inherited an unfinished project.
examples.cn: 委员会接手了一个没做完的项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因何丽特」——因何丽特得了遗产？因为她继承了老屋

root: 拉丁语 heres「继承人」加上 in- 构成 inhereditare「使成为继承人」，经古法语 enheriter 传入英语作 inherit；同根词有 heir、heritage、inheritance、heredity。十九世纪起又用于遗传学。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses share one image of handover: property after a death, a situation left by a predecessor, and traits passed through genes.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项共用一个「移交」意象：身后的财产、前任留下的局面，以及经基因传下的特征。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key and an account book pass from an old hand to a young one.
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙与账簿从老人的手交到年轻人手里。

branches.en: THE WILL: property passes at death, and the law records who receives it.
branches.cn: 遗嘱这条线：财产在身故时转移，法律记录由谁接受。

branches.en: THE TITLE: names and offices are inherited as readily as land.
branches.cn: 头衔这条线：姓氏与职位和土地一样可以被继承。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: a successor inherits whatever the predecessor left, good or bad.
branches.cn: 职位这条线：继任者接手前任留下的一切，无论好坏。

branches.en: THE BODY: genes hand down traits as families hand down land.
branches.cn: 身体这条线：基因传下特征，正如家族传下土地。

branches.en: THE THREAD: in every sense something arrives from the past and must be carried on.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：每个义项里都有东西从过去抵达，并须被延续。

intro.en: Inherit is a Latin prefix plus the Latin word for heir, reshaped in Old French and English.
intro.cn: inherit 是拉丁语前缀加拉丁语「继承人」一词，经古法语与英语改写而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin heres and inhereditare are recorded; the related heredity shows the same root in modern English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 heres 与 inhereditare 均有记录，现代英语的 heredity 显示同一词根。

items.example: It places someone into the heir's position.
items.exampleCN: 它把人放进继承人的位置。

items.example: The noun is the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词义的核心。

items.meaning: to make an heir, to bequeath
items.example: The verb from which the word descends.
The stem was shortened in French.
items.exampleCN: 这一词干在法语中被缩短。

items.example: The root survives as a word on its own.
The learned form of the same root.
items.exampleCN: 这是同一词根的书面形式。

items.example: A negative prefix reverses the act.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀把动作反了过来。

definition_en: very impressive and beautiful, or excellent
core_image: 夕阳把整片山谷染成金色
scene: 夕阳把山谷照得一片辉煌。 The sunset made the valley splendid.
sceneCN: 这里 splendid 是「壮丽的、辉煌的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：夕阳把山谷照得一片辉煌。

senses.title: Magnificent to see
senses.definition: magnificent and impressive to look at
senses.definitionCN: 看上去宏伟而令人赞叹的
senses.example: The sunset made the valley splendid.
senses.exampleCN: 夕阳把山谷照得一片辉煌。
senses.why: The core sense comes from shining beauty.
senses.whyCN: 最核心的义项源于光彩夺目的美。

senses.title: Very good
senses.definition: excellent, used especially in spoken praise
senses.definitionCN: 极好的，多用于口头称赞
senses.example: That is a splendid idea.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个绝妙的主意。
senses.why: The visual sense weakens into general praise.
senses.whyCN: 视觉义弱化，变成一般性的称赞。

senses.title: Rich in style
senses.definition: rich and impressive in style or decoration
senses.definitionCN: 风格或装饰富丽堂皇的
senses.example: The hall had a splendid ceiling.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅有一个华丽的天花板。
senses.why: The sense stays visual but moves to built things.
senses.whyCN: 仍属视觉义，但转向人造之物。

intro.en: Splendid comes from Latin splendidus, meaning shining.
intro.cn: splendid 来自拉丁语 splendidus，意为闪光的。

items.en: Splendere meant to shine or glow.
items.cn: splendere 意为发光、闪耀。

items.en: Splendidus described something bright and fine.
items.cn: splendidus 形容明亮而精美之物。

items.en: Splendid entered English as shining and fine.
items.cn: splendid 以「明亮精美」之义进入英语。

items.en: It broadened to mean magnificent.
items.cn: 词义扩展为「宏伟壮丽」。

items.en: It also became a polite word of praise.
items.cn: 它又成为礼貌的称赞用语。

note.en: Splendid is compared with look-alike words and words for beauty.
note.cn: 把 splendid 与形近词以及表示华美的词作比较。

entries.definition: of the inner self
not ordinary
to divide into parts
extremely impressive
very beautiful
very bright or clever

normalIntro.en: Splendid is light made into a compliment.
normalIntro.cn: splendid 是被说成赞美的光。

normal.en: What a splendid view!
normal.cn: 景色真壮丽！

normal.en: That is a splendid idea.
normal.cn: 那是个绝妙的主意。

normal.en: They live in a splendid house.
normal.cn: 他们住在一座华丽的房子里。

normal.en: The garden looks splendid in spring.
normal.cn: 春天的花园看起来美极了。

normal.en: You did a splendid job.
normal.cn: 你干得很棒。

abstract.en: Splendour is a light that stays after sunset.
abstract.cn: 辉煌，是日落之后仍留着的光。

abstract.en: Praise borrows the words of sunlight.
abstract.cn: 赞美借用了阳光的词汇。

abstract.en: The finest halls are quiet inside.
abstract.cn: 最华丽的厅堂，内里最安静。

examples.en: The sunset made the valley splendid.
examples.cn: 夕阳把山谷照得一片辉煌。

examples.en: That is a splendid idea.
examples.cn: 那是个绝妙的主意。

examples.en: The hall had a splendid ceiling.
examples.cn: 大厅有一个华丽的天花板。

dict_mnemonic.text: splendid 与 splendour（壮丽）同根，词根意为「发光」；splendid view 是壮丽景色，splendid idea 是绝妙主意；口语中常用作「极好的」。

root: 来自拉丁语 splendidus（闪光的），词根 splendere 意为发光，核心义由「光彩夺目」扩展到「壮丽」与「极好」。

sensesIntro.en: Splendid means magnificent to see, excellent, or rich in style.
sensesIntro.cn: splendid 指外观壮丽、极好，或风格华丽。

core.en: Light that makes people stop and look.
core.cn: 让人停下来看的光。

branches.en: Gold spreads over the valley.
branches.cn: 金色铺满山谷。

branches.en: A voice says, what a good idea.
branches.cn: 一个声音说，这主意真好。

branches.en: Carved ceilings catch the candlelight.
branches.cn: 雕花天花板接住烛光。

branches.en: Nature and craft both aim at glory.
branches.cn: 自然与工艺，都朝着辉煌。

branches.en: Praise and ornament share one brightness.
branches.cn: 赞美与装饰，共用一种明亮。

intro.en: Splendid forms comparison, nouns, and adverbs.
intro.cn: splendid 构成比较级、名词和副词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is splendere, to shine.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 splendere，意为发光。

items.example: The view grew splendider at dusk.
The splendidness of the scene struck us.
items.exampleCN: 景色的壮丽震撼了我们。

items.example: A splendorous dawn lit the sea.
items.exampleCN: 辉煌的黎明照亮了海面。

definition_zh: 昏倒；晕倒；微弱的；模糊的；虚弱的
definition_en: to lose consciousness for a short time; weak and not clear to see or hear; feeling weak and dizzy; slight and not strong
core_image: 眼前的光和声音一起变淡，人慢慢失去知觉
scene: 她因饥饿晕倒了。 She fainted from hunger.
sceneCN: 这里 faint 是「昏倒、晕倒」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她因饥饿晕倒了。

senses.title: To lose consciousness
senses.definition: to lose consciousness for a short time
senses.definitionCN: 短暂失去知觉
senses.example: He fainted in the hot room.
senses.exampleCN: 他在闷热的房间里晕倒了。
senses.why: The verb sense is the body switching off briefly.
senses.whyCN: 动词义是身体短暂「关机」。

senses.title: Weak and unclear
senses.definition: weak and not clear to see, hear, or smell
senses.definitionCN: 视觉、听觉或嗅觉上微弱而不清晰
senses.example: A faint light showed under the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门底下透出微弱的光。
senses.why: The weak signal is like consciousness almost gone.
senses.whyCN: 微弱信号就像意识几乎消失。

senses.title: Feeling weak
senses.definition: feeling weak and dizzy, as if about to faint
senses.definitionCN: 感到虚弱头晕，仿佛快要昏倒
senses.example: She felt faint after standing up quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 她猛地站起来后感到眩晕。
senses.why: The body approaches the state of fainting.
senses.whyCN: 身体正处于接近昏倒的状态。

senses.title: Slight
senses.definition: slight and not strong or likely
senses.definitionCN: 轻微、不强或可能性不大
senses.example: There is a faint hope that he will return.
senses.exampleCN: 他回来的希望很渺茫。
senses.why: A weak signal becomes a small chance or trace.
senses.whyCN: 微弱信号引申为渺小机会或痕迹。

intro.en: Faint comes from Old French feint, sluggish or pretended, from feindre, to feign.
intro.cn: faint 来自古法语 feint（无力的、假装的），源头 feindre（假装）。

items.en: Fingere means to shape or pretend.
items.cn: fingere 意为塑造或假装。

items.en: Feindre means to pretend or hesitate.
items.cn: feindre 意为假装或迟疑。

items.en: Faint means weak or weary.
items.cn: 中古英语中 faint 意为虚弱或疲惫。

items.en: The verb means to lose consciousness.
items.cn: 现代英语中动词义为失去知觉。

items.en: Faint also describes weak signals and slight chances.
items.cn: 当代英语中 faint 也描述微弱信号与渺小机会。

note.en: Faint means weak; feint is a deceptive move.
note.cn: faint 是虚弱的，feint 则是佯攻。

entries.definition: a movement meant to deceive
coloured liquid for surfaces
a very holy person
to lose consciousness
not bright or clear

normalIntro.en: Faint describes both the body going dark and signals growing weak.
normalIntro.cn: faint 既描述身体失去知觉，也描述信号变弱。

normal.en: She felt faint in the heat.
normal.cn: 她在高温中感到头晕。

normal.en: He fainted at the sight of blood.
normal.cn: 他一见血就晕倒了。

normal.en: A faint smell of smoke filled the room.
normal.cn: 房间里弥漫着淡淡的烟味。

normal.en: We heard a faint sound in the distance.
normal.cn: 我们听到远处有微弱的声音。

normal.en: There is a faint chance of rain.
normal.cn: 下雨的可能性很小。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp turned down to its lowest glow.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯被调到最暗的光。

abstract.en: Imagine the room tilting as your knees give way.
abstract.cn: 想象膝盖发软、房间倾斜。

abstract.en: Think of a hope as thin as a thread of smoke.
abstract.cn: 把希望想成细如烟丝。

examples.en: The hiker fainted from the heat.
examples.cn: 徒步者因高温晕倒了。

examples.en: There was a faint outline of a ship on the horizon.
examples.cn: 地平线上有一艘船的模糊轮廓。

examples.en: She gave a faint smile and left.
examples.cn: 她淡淡一笑便离开了。

dict_mnemonic.text: faint 原意是「无力的」，力气从身体退去会昏倒，光与声从感官退去就变得 faint。

root: faint 来自古法语 feint（无力的、假装的），源自拉丁语 fingere（塑造、假装），由「无力」引申出昏倒与微弱。

sensesIntro.en: Faint means to lose consciousness, or to be weak, unclear, dizzy, or slight.
sensesIntro.cn: faint 意为昏倒，或表示微弱、模糊、眩晕、轻微。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: senses dimming until the body switches off.
core.cn: 核心意象：感官变暗直到身体关机。

branches.en: The verb sense is losing consciousness.
branches.cn: 动词义是失去知觉。

branches.en: Signals become weak and unclear.
branches.cn: 信号变得微弱模糊。

branches.en: The body feels close to fainting.
branches.cn: 身体感到接近昏倒。

branches.en: Weakness becomes a slight chance or trace.
branches.cn: 微弱引申为渺小机会或痕迹。

branches.en: Feeling faint is the warning before fainting.
branches.cn: 眩晕是昏倒前的预警。

intro.en: Faint builds adverbs and nouns with -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: faint 通过 -ly 与 -ness 构成副词和名词。

latinIntro.en: Faint traces back through French to Latin fingere, to shape or pretend.
latinIntro.cn: faint 经由法语追溯到拉丁语 fingere（塑造、假装）。

items.meaning: to pass out or to be weak

items.example: He faints at the sight of blood.
Fainting can signal low blood pressure.
I do not have the faintest idea.
This task is not for the fainthearted.
items.exampleCN: 这项任务不适合胆小的人。

latinEntries.example: Fingere is the distant root of faint.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fingere 是 faint 的远源。
